HESS BRASS AN EDWARDS AN HOFFMAN xecutive Vice President The many effective merchan- ising programs created and di- ected by Stan Hoffman have ade an invaluable contribution to the current growth and success of Chess/Janus Records. He's been instrumental in revitalizing the label's image and in building the careers of many artists on the roster. Previous experience as head of his own independent distributor- ship gives Stan a unique insight into both sides of record merchan- dising. When planning new mar- keting campaigns he knows how it will work from the distributor's viewpoint. He can also help set realistic sales projections and see that they're met. Stan sets directions for cam- paigns and supervises the place- ment of radio and print ads. As though all that weren't enough, Stan is also general office man- ager, he maintains close contact with distributors and buyers and he oversees the day to day opera- tions of Chess/Janus. Marvin Schlachter appointed Stan executive vice president in March, 1972. Stan had distin- guished himself as director of merchandising since June 1971, when Chess/Janus was formed. He originally joined the company in January of that year as vice president and general manager of Dome Distributing, which at the time was owned by GRT Records. He had formerly been general manager of Schwartz Brothers, Inc. in Washington, D.C. for four years and he spent seven years as president and owner of the Balti- more -based distributorship Mar - nel of Maryland. He began as branch manager of Marnel for two years. He lives in Fort Lee, New Jer- sey with his wife Phyllis. Stan has two children from a previous mar- riage, 17 year -old Norma, who starts at college this fall, and 13 year -old Russell. They both live in Baltimore with their mother. Ten- nis and reading occupy whatever spare time Stan has from his many activities as executive vice president. ESMOND EDWARDS Vice President of Af3R Esmond Edwards is equally at home behind the control board in a recording studio, where he pro- duces such artists as Chuck Berry and Jack McDuff, and the executive desk, where he directs the A & R activities of Chess/ Janus Records. Edwards began in the music FELD SCERBO business as a clerk at Prestige Records. Within five years he was the label's vice president. Es pro- duced "Don't Go To Strangers" by Etta Jones, "Canadian Sunset" by Gene Ammonds and many oth- er records for Prestige before moving to Chess Records, where he spent five years as head of jazz A & R. His credits there in- clude Ramsey Lewis' biggest hits and the creation of the Soulful Strings. Edwards then replaced Creed Taylor as head of Verve Records. He was with Columbia briefly be- fore joining Polydor Records as executive assistant to Jerry Schoenbaum and, in late 1970, rejoined Chess Records as vice president of A & R for all the company's labels. When Marvin Schlachter reorganized the Chess and Janus companies, in June of 1971, Esmond Edwards assumed the responsibilities of A & R chief for the combined Chess/Janus Record company. His hobbies are photography, which has resulted in many album covers, and playing the guitar. Esmond lives in New Rochelle with his wife Bonita and seven year -old son Evan. IRVING FELD Vice Pres. of Administration Overseeing the vital financial picture for Chess/Janus Records is Irving Feld. He balances the budget to provide the label with maximum returns on their ex- penditures. A Certified Public Accountant, Irving comes to Chess/Janus from his position as account man- ager for S. D. Leidesdorf & Co., tenth largest international ac- counting firm. In this capacity, Feld was active in the financial management of several of the firm's large entertainment indus- try clients. A graduate of City College of New York, Irving Feld first joined the noted accounting firm of J. K. Lasser before going with Leides- dorf. He lives with his wife Ro- berta, daughter Shari, 6, and son Jeffrey, 2, in Syosset on Long Is- land. Tennis, reading and garden- ing are among his hobbies. BOB SCERBO Dir. of Production E4 Intl Operations With Janus Records from the very beginning, Bob Scerbo now handles two formidable areas for Chess/Janus with aplomb. His production department is one of the busiest in the company, get- ting out a steady flow of album RILEY covers and promotional material. Bob also directs the liaison with the label's many overseas affil- iates, an especially important area in view of the international interest in Chess/Janus product. Scerbo's well rounded music business background includes po- sitions as director of production and director of international op- erations at Musicor Records for three and 3 years assistant pro- duction director at United Artists Records. Immediately prior to joining Janus, Bob was a sales representative for the County Box and Album Company, manufac- turers of album jackets. Away from the office, Bob en- joys all forms of sports, especially hockey and basketball. He and his wife Adrianne live in New City in Rockland County with their four - month old daughter Victoria Leigh. AL RILEY National Promotion Dir. With product exposure one of the key factors in the "hit" for- mula, the brilliant promotional talents of Al Riley have made a substantial contribution to the success Chess/Janus has enjoyed on both the soul and pop charts. Whether visiting disk jockies in - person or maintaining close con- tact with them on the phone, Al uses his quiet persuation with ex- traordinary effectiveness. R & B promotion director of Janus Records since June of 1970, Riley became involved with Chess when the two companies merged a year later. He was named national promotion direc- tor of the combined labels in De- cember of 1971. Riley spent six years with Lib- erty Records and its affiliate labels, leaving as national pro- motion director for Minit/Blue Note/Solid State Records. He be- gan as a clerk at Liberty and sub- sequently rose to salesman in the greater New York area, branch promotion man, east coast re- gional promotion director for Blue Note/Solid State Records and na- tional sales and promotion direc- tor for Minit Records before join- ing Janus. His hobbies include football, baseball, tennis and golf. Al has two daughters, Kyle, 13, and Jen- nifer, 7, from an earlier marriage. He lives in Rego Park, New York. Symposium NEW YORK -A large assemblage of recording industry brass will be attending the May 18-20 weekend convention and meeting of New York State's three regional associations (MONY, Westchester Guild and New York State Operators Guild). Ben Chicofsky, whose MONY offices spearhead the planning for this annu- al event (to take place at the Mt. Airy Lodge in the Poconos) advised that a symposium on problems mutu- ally confronting the record and Wurlitzer Singles for Nostalgia (Continued) press and broadcast media at large, and are certain to gain maximum publicity for all as a result." Palmer advised that such a press reception is not unprededented. Be- fore the World War II machine mori- torium, a Wurlitzer jukebox was in- troduced in a similiar manner. The sensational nature of the new "an- tique' Jukebox, Palmer felt, called for it to happen again. The event will include a reveal and inspection of the machine, an old-time free lunch complete with flowing tap beer-even waiters decked in period attire. Several showbiz performers will at- tend, including Theresa Brewer who's 'Music, Music, Music' golden standard typifies the theme of the day. Concerning the actual marketing of the unit to the operating industry, Palmer advised that operators will be able to merchandise the unique unit to maximum advantage both in new and existing locations. To further stimulate the idea, Palmer has signed Gold -Mor Distributing to assemble two 25 disk 45 rpm record packs-one containing nostalgic hits of the 30's and 40's, the second rock from the 50's and 60's. "Gold-Mor's selections, and they took some time to select and assemble from the various labels, is mag- nificent," Palmer declared. "If anyone doubts the marketing value of nostal- gia, they've just got to listen to these tunes on this jukebox and they'll be convinced. And I don't care what the age or the place is. We've got it for everyone." MOA Meet (Continued) In his concluding remarks Fred Granger said, "After about nine years' service with MOA, I am still very much impressed with the associ- ation's board of directors for the very professional, businesslike manner in which the board meetings are con- ducted. Each and every member serves with distinction and I am proud to be associated with such a distinguished group." jukebox business will take place the evening of May 18th. Topics to be aired include record quality control, time length and sampling service. Record people will be most inter- ested to learn what they may do to further stimulate the operator's busi- ness, and are anxious to discover which promotional and service steps they may try to establish a better relationship between the two indus- tries. Chicofsky advised that among the major labels to be represented are: RCA, Columbia, Epic, United Artists, MCA Group, A&M and Mercury. All told, over 200 tradesmen and their wives will be attending the weekend event. Chicofsky advised at press time that 80% of the room block in the Mt. Airy's Regency Building have been reserved already and that late starters had better notify this office this week if they wish to at- tend. Triangle Appoints Treasurer Asst. -tosx KOtiOtiIiQ{}LtiOi}=i}={ }' }pt}}çt cash box / talent on stage xnosfo4sot1o4)=X1o43<=tld=iso4s=4)o:1ot3o43t uK==es=XXots 00C I , ambalra Mason Natural Four MISTER KELLY'S CHICAGO - Buddah songstress Barbara Mason has enjoyed much success as a re- cording artist with considerable chart exposure, most notably in the r&b vein. Her distinctive soul style lends itself well to the material she per- forms in the blues category; however, as proven during her Mister Kelly's engagement, she is equally adept at performing the more pop -oriented material. "I Love You More Today Than Yesterday," "Rainy Days And Mondays," "Fever," "Yes I'm Ready" (the tune which first brought her disk prominence) and "Give Me Your Love" (a recent chart item) were some of her standout offerings. Also on the bill was a very lively vocal group called The Natural Four, comparative newcomers, discovered by Curtis Mayfield and Mary Stuart of Curtom Records. The group gained some recognition with their initial Curtom release "Things Will Be Bet- ter Tomorrow" and are currently in- troducing their follow-up "Eddie You Should Know Better." Both numbers were included in their repertoire, along with "Too Late," "Daydream- ing" and others. On some tunes, the lead singer displayed a slight similar- ity in style to Curtis Mayfield. The group's delivery is energetic and their performance very entertaining. C.C. 2001 Space Concert FELT FORUM, NYC - CTI Rec- ords presented Deodato and Airto (making their debuts) and the talents of three veteran jazzmen-Freddie Hubbard, Stanley Turrentine and Eric Gale in a recent program, billed as a "2001 Space Concert." The highlight and finale of the evening was Deodato and his nine piece group. They performed with such vigor and total dedication, the audience began dancing in the aisles. The group got a well -deserved stand- ing ovation. Deodato's style is Latin/ - rock with jazz undercurrents com- bined with a dash of originality. A version of the classic "Baubles, Ban- gles and Beads" proved imaginative and exciting. Of course, the current hit, "Also Sprach Zarathustra" cli- maxed the event. It is difficult to fault the musicians and their music. But, all of the enthu- siasm generated was swept away by the interminably long delays between the sets. The mellow tones of Freddie Hubbard offered a nice change of pace. Accompanied by such notables as Ron Carter, Jack Dejohnette, Eric Gale and Stanley Turrentine, Freddie, in rare and usual cool form, got the Forum rocking "First Light," from his Grammy award winning LP of the same name was played with such dy- namism, it heralded an encoure. Solos by Eric Gale offered a mellow -smooth rendition of the Roberta Flack hit, "Killing Me Softly With His Song." Also, a Turrentine sax solo was in a get down groove. Opening the program was the new- ly reformed Airto group. Airto's mu- sic can be best described as a blend of Latin/jazz/rock with considerable chanting-somewhat similar to Indian and African folk songs. Backed by four musicians and his wife, Flora Purim, Airto and the group should continue to grow in stature. Most in- teresting were the numerous Brazilian percussion instruments Airto and Flora used. We understand that Airto made these. Although the talent presented in this "2001 Space Concert" was of high caliber, considerably more preparation in organizing the pro- gram would have made a wail of a difference. d.d. Loggins & Messina Sandy Denny CAPITOL THEATRE, N.J. - In just a short year and a half, Kenny Log- gins and Jim Messina have blossomed into established headlining stars, playing before jam-packed concert halls wherever they perform. Maintaining their customary format. Loggins gently opened the set with easy-going acoustic material, featuring "House at Poo Corner," and "Danny's Song." His pleasant vocals and amiable rapport with the young fans were as soothing as the melodies and totally captivating. The good vibes continued to swell when Jim Messina and the remaining group members soon joined Loggins. The transformation from quiet living room atmosphere to that of a swing- ing country hoedown was immediate. As always, Messina's guitar work was tasty, and his vocals a perfect com- plement with Loggins. From start to finish, the hand was warm, loose. and full of good time music like "Holiday Hotel," and "Vahevella." Extended versions of "Angry Eyes," and the expected oncore of "Your Mama Don't Dance," were amazingly tight, and left every listener truly satisfied. A&M's Sandy Denny never really had a chance as the more than anxi- ous L&M crowd treated her with rude response. After finishing but a few numbers, and obviously a little shak- en over the lack of courtesy any ar- tist deserves, Miss Denny decided to call it quits and walked off the stage. m.a. Odetta ill Quateman UPSTAIRS AT MAX'S, NYC - Odetta made her long-standing en- trance, singing acapella as she ap- proached the stage. It's always inter- esting to see what she's into. Not to mention mindblowing. Odetta is now backed by Her Nash- ville Huggies, but she's not singin' 'em country as the moniker might imply. Most of the tunes are stan- dards from her repertory of folk- song, given appropriate arrangements without making them simple "folk- rock" or "folk pap" (as is often the case when traditional melodies are "updated"). Odetta still sings her heart out into the open. "I feel posi- tively delicious tonight," she told the crowd. "I'm goin' to stand here mak- in' love to you and I don't want you to be the passive lover." Symbolical- ly, but very definitely, the deep affec- tion was returned a hundred fold. The unconventionally beautiful black woman who commands undeniable re- spect from the music community as a whole spent some time talking about an idea she has for an LP, "Songs You Learned To Hate In School" and then proceeded to make you love them. Hopefully a label will take her up on the concept, as she is between contracts at present and deserves to be recorded now more than ever. Columbia's new singer/composer from Chicago, Bill Quateman, began his set a bit shaky, but continued to build himself into a most entertaining good time. His vocals are akin to Steve Stills, but his material is more broadly personal and expressive. His single "Only Love" was the set's high point, in a dead heat with his closing "God Bless Everybody." On the latter, he had no trouble soliciting audience participation without ap- pearing obvious about it. That in it- self leads one to believe that in time, Quateman will succeed in a big way. His ability to move with ease from guitar to piano and his stage presence (resembling a handsomer, more to- gether Michael J. Pollard) are also working towards that end. r.a. War LONG BEACH (CALIF.) ARENA - United Artist's recording group War began by playing free concerts in the ghettos of Watts and in four years have moved on to playing to audi- ences like Long Beach of over eight thousand people. In their million sel- ler "The World Is a Ghetto" there's a line that goes. "... Wonder if I'll find happiness." Well, the gross to this gig was over $45,000, so apparently they have found happiness-and so has their proficient management, Far Out Productions. The adept artilery is made up of Lee Oscar on harmonica (one of the best around), Howard Scott on gui- tar, Papa Dee Allen on percussion, Harold Brown playing drums, Lonnie Jordan keyboard, and B. B. Dickerson on bass-all contributing vocals. They are clearly seasoned performers who know how to satisfy an audience. Their encoure alone was nearly 45 minutes long. War opened with their "Gypsy Man" and segued into hits like "Ghet- to," "Cisco Kid" and "Slipping into Darkness." Some of their numbers are a little too stretched out time -wise Long jams are best left to intimate jazz clubs or places where people can dance. It's very difficult getting off to a lengthy version of a top -forty hit confined to a seat within a massive arena. Nevertheless their flawless per- formance demonstrated how War won the west during the kick off of their national spring tour. The group has solidly proved itself via records and concerts, and next don't be surprised if they score a movie. They'd be per- fect for it. r.b. Harold Melvin & The I:; lue Notes COPA, NYC - Harold Melvin & The Blue Notes, currently headlining at the famed show spot, are truly mag- nificent performers. They have got it together! The show, from the opening chord, is charged with get down ex- citement. The group, backed by seven pieces, most decidedly turns you on with tremendous renditions of, "Anybody Know What Time It Is," "What's Happenin' Brother" and, "If You Don't Know Me By Now," and they're only opening teasers. Their backup rhythm section is great, especially Jerry Jones on drums. Pendergast, doing lead vocalist chores on many of the tunes, can lay an onlooker out! The pace does get lowdown and funky with a soul ver- sion of, "Can't Get Next To You." Then, without a break and with one of the most beautifully executed chord changes, the group swings into, "Mercy, Mercy." What a tribute to Marvelous Mary (Marvin Gaye). "I Miss You" and "Follow Me," creates more sheer enjoyment. "Yesterday I Had The Blues," a current big hit, was also given a topnotch reading. Harold Melvin & The Blues Notes are high-energy soul performers. Whether they turn it on before an Apollo audience, or do their thing at the Copa, they do turn you on and won't let you go; it's their style and they know what it takes. All one has to do is sit back and enjoy the Blue Notes. With their special brand of soul and performing talents, one can be assured of one helluva musical event. Sal Richards, on the bill, opens the show with some chatter and song. But, the Blue Notes are the top card. d.d. Edgar Winter CAPITOL THEATRE, N.J. - The Edgar Winter Group walked onto the Capitol stage and were immediately overwhelmed by a thunderous ovation that with every song, became a deafening roar of noisy music and hysterical young fans. In his days with White Trash, Edgar and company were extremely tight and had real class. Using no gimmicks, they were slick and one of the best precisioned rock and roll bands around. Now, there is a new band, and Win- ter has found the hard driving musci- ans he has always wanted for his style of music. Ronnie Montrose plays lead guitar, Dan Hartman basss, and Chuck Ruff drums. They are just as much energy plus as Winter and each possesses great talent. But there is something missing. Unfortunately, at this performance, the amps were up full volume as the quartet struggled with each other to be heard. There was an added light show with other effects that appeared to be thrown together at the last minute and this made the show more offensive. But the kids really loved it as the group wailed on and on through "To- bacco Road." "Let's Get it On." and "Rock and Roll Boogie Woogie Blues." "Frankenstein," their latest single, was definitely the strongest number of the set, giving good indi- cation of what this band can really do. Perhaps it was just an off evening because the Edger Winter Group can most certainly become a powerful force in rock and roll. However, the gimmitry and noisy display seen and heard at this concert must be worked out, especially when it costs them the tightness, precision, and class that is usually their trademark. m.a. J. Geils David .) > and lue SANTA MONICA CIVIC - Peter Wolf (we're not fabling here), the lead singer of the J. Geils Band, came on the stage and told his sr. audience that there are two kinds of people in the world: the lazies and the crazies. The J. Geils Band happens to be any- thing but lazy. They may, however, be considered a little carzy, but their formidable music has a way of mak- ing "a feeling of unabashed crazy" seem ingratiating by the end of the evening. The group is into loud, rau- cous rhythm and blues reminiscent of Mitch Ryder at his peak. Wolf is a rapacious showman. He has the rare know-how to exorcise even the lazies." The group opened with "First I Look at the Purse," an old Contours tune, and right away con- vinced their crowd they had bought tickets to a winning purse. The sextet contains along with Peter, Seth Just - man on keyboard, J. (Jolter) Geils on guitar, Magic Dick on harp, Daniel Klein on bass, and Stephen Bladd on drums. Other devastating tunes in- cluded "Southside Shuffle" (should be a single), "Make Up Your Mind," and "Give It to Me" (their current sin- gle). Also on the bill was David Blue, new Asylum artist. Blue sang folk and country pop songs under a blue spot. It was clear that the audience, just as soon he, disappeared into the blue that was until Graham Nash came out to sing with him. Blue is very talented but it also became clear that he should be the lead singer in a group. His "Outlaw Man" with har- monizing by Nash sounds like a hit. Let's look for the D. Blue Band. r.b. B'nai B'rith Awards Go To King, Merman NEW YORK - B. B. King and Ethel Merman will. be presented the Human- itarian Award and the Creative Achievement Award, respectively, at the Music and Performing Arts Lodge of B'nai B'rith Dinner on Saturday, June 9. The announcement, made by lodge president Ira Moss, noted that this is the 9th Annual Awards Dinner Dance to be held since 1965 honoring some of the giants in the business and at the same time raising funds for B'nai B'rith and its affiliated causes. The affair, which will be held in the Tri- anon Ballroom of the New York Hil- ton Hotel, was previously honored such personalities as James Brown, William B. Williams, Sammy Davis, Jr., Bill Graham and Jane Pickens with the Humanitarian Award. Previ- ous recipients of the Creative Achievement Award have been Sheldon Harnick, Jerry Bock and Joseph Stein, Jerry Herman, Fred Ebb and John Kander, Burt Bachar - ach and Hal David, Dionne Warwick and, most recently, Henry Mancini in 1972. As usual, the Lodge's own Paul Livert Orchestra will provide music for the entire evening. The black tie affair, is being co- chaired by Ken Rosenbloom, Toby Pi- eniek and Milt Suchin. Tickets for the dinner -dance are available at $50.00 per person with group seating avail- able for parties of 10 or 12. Ticket information and reservations may be had by calling George Levy at (212) 786-3337. MCA, Sound Image To Tour `Tommy' HOLLYWOOD - MCA and Sound Image, Inc. are co -producing and pre- senting an elaborate concert produc- tion of the rock opera "Tommy," writ- ten by Pete Townshend and the Who, to tour nationwide and Canada, ac- cording to Raphael Etkes, vice presi- dent, Universal Pictures. The tour, booked by CMA, premieres - on July 20 for one week in Chicago at the Auditorium Theater and stars Teddy Neely in the title role. Neely, who portrays the role of "Jesus" in the soon -to -be -released Universal film "Jesus Christ Super- star," directed by Norman Jewison, also appeared in the role in the stage presentation of "Superstar" last sum- mer at Universal's outdoor Amphi- theatre. The entire concert production of "Tommy" is supervised by Jules Fisher. Stigwood Wins Decision On Film 'Superstar' NEW YORK - U. S. District Judge Carl B. Rubin entered an order in the U. S. District Court on May 3 for the Southern District of Ohio, eastern di- vision, permanently enjoining defen- dants Pierre Robin and The Repertory Company of American Inc. from pro- ceeding with threatened plans to make a movie version of "Jesus Christ-Superstar." The court also granted the motions of The Robert Stigwood Group Ltd. et al. for a sum- mary judgment, rejecting the defen- dants contention that the underlying conception of "Superstar" was pirat- ed from The Passover Plot, a book by Dr. Hugh Schonfield. The final judgment continues a pre- liminary injunction entered late last Dec. restraining defendant Robin and his agents from proceeding with plans for the "Superstar" film "in complete disregard of plaintiffs simi- lar plans, sizeable capital investment, and presumptively valid copy- rights." Ruling In granting Stigwood the motion for summary judgment, the court re- jected the defendants contention that the Leeds copyright claims were in- valid because the underlying concep- tion of "Jesus Christ-Superstar" was plagiarized from The Passover Plot, and ruled that the ideas embodied in "Jesus Christ-Superstar" are derived from an independant source in the public domain, namely the Bible. In support of its opinion, the court cited its complete agreement with the hold- ing of Stigwood v. O'Reilly: It is clear that the plaintiffs' lyrics are original, highly creative, and even controversial, expressions of the Bi- blical passages. As such, they are within the protection of the Copy- right Act. The court also held for Stigwood that the title "Jesus Christ- Superstar" has developed a secondary significance in the public's mind in connection with the opera as a whole, and thus enjoined the defendants from "directly or indirectly advertis- ing or in any way representing any presentation as being from `Jesus Christ-Superstar,' or from making or attempting to make a motion pic- ture or television production of the same." Plaintiffs were represented by Rob- ert C. Osterberg of Abeles, Clark and Osterberg. London Looks To Top Spring/ Summer Sales NEW YORK - London Records is preparing for its biggest spring and summer ever, releasing albums cover- ing the "vast extent of the musical rainbow." London vice president of sales and marketing Herb Goldfarb, in announcing the huge release, also noted that every promotional and merchandising scheme available will be used to push the new albums throughout the spring and summer. Hot on the recent release of Al Green's latest "Call Me," London will be releasing new LP's by Tom Jones, Mantovani, Savoy Brown, Chris Youlden, Ronnie Aldrich, Tony Rand- all and Jack Klugman-"The Odd Couple Sings"-and Keef Harlety, along with the five -record set of Wagner's "Parsifal" with Sir Georg Solti conducting. Sir Georg, by the way, was the subject of a recent Time Magazine cover story. Shortly thereafter, London will strike again with new albums by En- gelbert Humperdinck, Z.Z. Top, and Chicken Shack, plus there will be a double-barreled UK Records release (distributed by London) of Ips by Jonathan King and Tina Harvey. Further, the label will present togeth- er on record for the first time a dou- ble live album by Richard Tucker and Robert Merrill, and, completing the release, numerous operas and classics are scheduled for issue on the Stereo Treasury label series. `Flipside' Set Thru Mid July NEW YORK - Marks/Aucoin Pro- ductions has announced the program- ming schedule through July 7 for "Flipside" the half-hour TV show which features a different record com- pany executive each week with two of his artists. The series will be seen on WNEW in New York and on KNBC in Los An- geles in the following order: Bell Rec- ords president Larry Uttal with The Fifth Dimension on May 26; Neil Bo- gart president of The Buddah Group with guest artists Curtis Mayfield and Sha Na Na on June 2; Motown Rec- ords president Ewart Abner with Stevie Wonder and Wonderlove on June 9; Jimmy Ienner, Co -President of C.A.M. Productions with the Rasp- berries on June 16. On June 23, independent producer Rick Derringer will appear with Ed- gar Winter and The Edgar Winter Group; John Lennon will appear with Yoko and with The Elephants Memory on June 30 and the July 7 program will feature Joel Dorn of Atlantic Rec- ords with songstress Roberta Flack and Yusef Lateef. Lott To Atl. Jazz Promo NEW YORK - Henry Allen Atlantic Records vice president of promotion has announced the appointment of Alan Lott as national promotion di- rector of jazz product. Lott comes to Atlantic from Warner-Elektra-Atlan- tic where he served as regional pro- motion coordinator. Lott will be responsible for expan- sion of jazz programming at the pro- gressive and rhythm and blues level as well as at jazz oriented stations. The appointment ties in with Atlan- tic's dedicating May as jazz month and their 10 LP release. He is now in the midst of mapping out a new cam- paign for the new Les McCann "Live At Montreux", Rahsaan Roland Kirk "Prepare Thyself To Deal With A Miracle", Herbie Mann "Hold On I'm Comin' ", and Eddie Harris "Excur- sions" LP's. He will work closely with Atlantic's vice president and producer, Joel Dorn, and producer, Michael Cus- cuna. Justice Dept. Asks Stiffer Pirate Penalty WASHINGTON, D. C. - The De- partment of Justice has asked Con- gress to increase the penalties for the illicit duplication of copyrighted sound recordings. The proposal by the Justice Depart- ment would make infringing of a copy- righted sound recording a felony pun- ishable by up to three years in jail and a fine of up to $25,000. Under the current law, such infringement is a misdemeanor punishable by up to one year in jail and/or a fine of up to $1,000. The Justice Department's proposal is contained in a bill (S.1400) now be- fore Congress that would revise and update the entire U. S. Criminal Code. The bill was introduced by Sen. Roman Hruska (R-Neb.), ranking Republican on the Senate Judiciary Committee. The Justice Department's backing of stiffer penalties for record and tape piracy is contained in a letter by Jo- seph T. Sneed, deputy attorney gen- eral. Sneed was responding to a letter from Sen. John L. McClellan, chair- man of the copyright subcommittee, who expressed his concern over the es- calation of the volume of illegal du- plication of sound recordings in viola- tion of the Amendment to the Copy- right Act which became effective February 15, 1972. Sneed Replies Sneed replied that the Justice De- partment has already "instituted a vigorous program to implement the provisions" of the current law, and said the Department would "urge even greater investigative efforts" by the Federal Bureau of Investigation. The Senate Subcommittee on Criminal Law and Procedures, also chaired by Sen. McClellan, has already started hearings on S.1400 and S.1, a similar bill introduced earlier in the year. Several weeks of additional hear- ings are scheduled. So far, under the Justice Depart- ment's enforcement program, one pi- rate has been convicted and indict- ments have been handed up against two others, one of whom has been charged with 48 counts of infringing on copyrighted recordings. Stanley M. Gortikov, President of RIAA, said that increasing penalties for the piracy of recordings would pro- vide an important new weapon in the battle against illegal duplicators. Agents Arrest Pirate Suspect In Tennessee NASHVILLE - Agents of the Ten- nessee Bureau of Criminal Identifica- tion arrested a North Carolina man here on charges of pirating long-play- ing phonograph records containing hit country and western material. Agents seized 9,000 albums, which they described as the final part of an 80,000 -album order that had been placed with a pressing plant here by Omega Sales of Atlanta. Omega was said to have contracted for these rec- ords to be pressed at a price of $23,- 000. Arrested for having violated the Tennessee anti -piracy statute was Michael Jeffrey Lynn, 33, of Charlotte, N.C. Lynn, who described himself as "self-employed," was released after posting a bond of $1,000. A pressing plant here reported that it had been fabricating the albums from masters supplied by the Atlanta firm and did not become aware that the recordings were pirated versions until 71,000 of the 80,000 ordered had been completed and delivered. Plant officials thereupon notified law en- forcement authorities. Lynn was taken into custody at the pressing plant when he arrived with a check for $11,- 000 to pick up the balance of the order. Manu Dibango, who has created a sensation w'th his, "Soul Makossa", was born in Douala, Cameroun, in 1934. Like many of his American colleagues, Manu came into contact with music at church meetings; then at 15 years of age he started piano lessons while in Europe. In the summer of '53, Manu was a counselor at a children's camp for young Africans. Manu was offered a saxaphone as a gift; from that moment, Manu turned resolutely to music. In 1960, he met Congolese musicians, then decided to return to African Music. Returning to Africa, Manu rediscovered the roots of his musical heritage and let this feed his imagination. He then turned to composing and his career has been on the ascendency . . . London, England based Contempo Records, formed in January 1973, is concentrating on the creation of new product. WB Markets Six Albums NEW YORK - Warner Bros. Rec- ords is releasing six new albums. They include "Sondheim-A Musical Tribute," containing performances from the Mar. 11 tribute to com- poser -lyricist Stephen Sondheim in New York. It's a 2 -LP set. Other sets include "For Your Pleasure" by Roxy Music, Tower of Power, "Maldoon." singer/songwriter Clive Maldoon, "Sittin' on Top of the World," Dean Martin and "Summer," featuring the San Sebastian Strings with words by Rod McKuen and mu- sic by Anita Kerr. Blue Note's All -Time LP; `Black Byrd' HOLLYWOOD - "Black Byrd," re- cently -released album by Donald Byrd, has achieved the milestone of becoming the biggest selling LP in the history of Blue Note Records, the jazz arm of United Artists Records, according to Eddie Levine, Blue Note's national sales and promo manager. The collection was issued last Feb. It has achieved best seller status, Le- vine says, in such key markets as New York, Baltimore, Washington, Philadelphia, Detroit, and Chicago, and is spreading broadly throughout the nation. Another plus factor in the sales pattern of "Black Byrd" is the growing MOR airplay from such ar- eas as Philadelphia, St. Louis, Kan- sas City and San Francisco. Levine reports Blue Note sales at an all-time peak with Lou Donald - son's "Sophisticated Lou," Alphonze Mouzon's "The Essence of Mystery" and Horace Silver's "In Pursuit Of The 27th Man," all joining "Black Byrd" as top movers in LP retail outlets from coast -to -coast. Bell Promo On Tony Orlando 'Look-Alikes' NEW YORK - Bell Records has launched a major, promotional "Look -Alive" contest backed by heavy multi -media advertising, public- ity and promo in conjunction with Dawn's starring engagement at New York's Copacabana. Recently number 1 with their million -selling single, "Tie A Yellow Ribbon Round The Ole Oak Tree," the group will headline at the famed nightery from June 7-16. The contest to find six look-alikes for Tony Orlando, lead singer of the group, is open to all students presently enrolled in high schools, junior colleges and colleges in the greater New York Metropolitan Area. It culminates on Friday, June 15, when six winners and their dates will be Tony's guests at the Copa. Already moving into high gear, Bell launched its Tony Orlando look - alike contest in mid -May with the mass mailing of the contest an- nouncement and rules, photos and bio material to every high school, junior college and college in the New York Metropolitan area including Long Is- land, Connecticut and New Jersey. Immediate follow-up includes ad- vertising in selected school papers and radio spots on both school and local radio stations. Bell has printed 5,000 specially designed contest flyers which are now being distributed on school campuses and through retail record outlets throughout the Metro- politan area. Dawn's Copa opening will gain further impetus from a "Rockin The Palace" segment taped on the Coast in mid -May which will be aired on ABC-TV on June 6 and a taped ap- pearance on the CBS -TV Mike Douglas Show, set for June 7. Tiger Tail Kiddie Line Mkt Expansion NEW YORK - The catalog of Tiger Tail Jigsaw Puzzle children's records, which now numbers over 25 titles encompassing a wide range of en- tertainment and instruction material for three to nine years old, is expand- ing its marketing base. Distributed by Audio Fidelity Rec- ords, Tiger Tail has been marketed up till now in traditional record out- lets, but is moving toward expanded representation in the toy depart- ments of chain store, supermarket and discount toy outlets. Audio Fidelity exec vice president Harold Drayson states that catalogs and display material are available and he is interested in inquiries from sales reps covering potential Tiger Tail outlets. Drayson also notes that many of the Tiger Tail titles are "ideally" suited to premiums and he is considering expanded activity in that area. Tiger Tail's recorded songs and stories are packaged in covers pre- cut as jigsaw puzzles thereby com- bining a record album and a game for the suggested list price of $1.98. Farrell Jingle Div. On Coast In Full Swing HOLLYWOOD - The Commercial Division of the Wes Farrell Organi- zation, which has been successfully producing music for commercials from its headquarters in New York, is now also in full-scale operation on the west coast under Tony Asher, head of the commercial division's west coast office. The Los Angeles office, in its first month of operation, has produced music for commercials for such prod- ucts as Instant Maxwell House Coffee, Mattel Toys and San Diego Trust. "The reaction so far is terrific," says 33 -year -old Asher, the former creative supervisor for Ogilvy/Ma- ther, Inc. "We are offering something unique-a single source of advertis- ing music in many different styles by our many different writers." The Wes Farrell Organization of companies encompasses music pro- duction and publishing companies housing a stable of young com- posers. These songwriters, who are writing hit records, are the same ones writing the commercial music, according to Asher. Asher is currently preparing a mailing to local area advertising agencies and potential users of music in commercials of a demo tape of spots that have been produced by the new west coast division. "Our attrac- tion to the advertising community," says Asher, "is the Wes Farrell Or- ganization's total involvement in all areas of the music business. This en- ables us the flexibility to produce demo jingles considerably faster and more economically." The west coast office of WFO's commercial division has been oper- ating since the beginning of April in new offices at 9200 Sunset Blvd. in Los Angeles. Golden Offers `Sawyer' Set NEW YORK - Golden Recrods has released an LP adaptation of Mark Twain's "Tom Sawyer" utilizing songs from the United Artists film. Produced by Ralph Stein, the album features an adaptation of the book by Sid Frank, with narration by Ear- ly Williams of Nashville. The album is also available on 8 -track and cas- sette configurations. Pregnancy Cancels Tour By Melanie NEW YORK - Neighborhood Rec- ords star Melanie has been forced to cancel her tour plans because of her pregnancy (her baby is due in Oct.). Her husband is Peter Schekeryk. Melanie's latest Neighborhood re- lease, "Melanie At Carnegie Hall," contains Melanie's past and present songs, including material not previ- ously available. Melanie plans on re- leasing a new album around Nov. New Pub. Co. HOLLYWOOD - Nightclub and re- cording artist Sir James "Jimmy" Randolph and his personal manager, Albert Fill, have formed Ranjay Mu- sic Publishing Co. to publish Ran- dolph's original music compositions as well as other writer -composers. First published tune for the new company is "High Road," the flip side of Ran- dolph's just -released Motown single, "Plainsville, U.S.A." Landmark Inks Singer For LP's NEW YORK - Landmark Enter- prises signed singer Joseph Neal to a recording contract for three albums, the first of which will be out in Nov., reports Bob McDevitt, a Landmark exec. Produc- tion, he added, will be "under the direct supervision of Jim Fragale, who produced Melba Moore's albums, including her hit single, `I Got Love'." J. The seminar concentrates on the ap- plication of modern audio design techniques and is intended for de- sign, studio, maintenance and sound system engineers. Audio System Design has been suc- cessful as a three-week, 70 -hour course. "The condensed course was created to meet the needs of engi- neers who were unable to attend the full course," said Iry Diehl, co- founder of the Institute. The seminar is an intensive study of practical systems engineering. It covers practical theory and applica- tion of modern design techniques which employ the "gain block" and constant voltage approach, as well as traditional methods of inpedance matching, thermal noise evaluation and grounding practice. Total fee for the seminar is $295.00. This covers cost of texts and all other printed materials. Student comprehension is aided by texts, a complete book of lecture notes and extensive reference materials. For information and registration, contact Iry Diehl at the Institute of Audio Research, Inc., 64 University Place, New York, 10003, 212/677-7580. Deadline for registration in the sem- inar is July 11, 1973. 18 Cash Box -June 9, 1973 www.americanradiohistory.com

BE SURE TO CHECK BUSINESS CLASSIFICATION ABOVE ( USlll I)OX' ' Round The Route CHICAGO CHATTER From the local newspapers comes word of a proposal, currently under consider- ation, to build an amusement park -fun center in the vicinity of the Northwest Tollway, about 45 miles from the Chicago downtown area. If plans materialize the complex would be built on 800 acres of land and would serve northern Illinois, southern Wisconsin and northwest Indiana. J. F. FRANTZ MFG. CO. prexy John Frantz items that his "U. S. Marshall" gun has been doing big business of late, not only domestically but, most especially, in the foreign markets! Since late last year the Frantz line has been handled by Nova of Germany. The gun's been selling beautifully in Europe, according to John, "and we couldn't be more pleased about it," he said, adding that "Canada is also a very good market for us." ROCK -OLA MFG. CORP.'S executive veepee Ed Doris just got back from a business trip to Venezuela ... Ad manager George Hincker returned to his office last week after attending the Virginia -Carolinas vending convention in Myrtle Beach, So. Carolina ... Earlier this month the Rock -Ola people entertained a very distinguished visitor, and friend, Mr. Adickes who was in from Germany to spend some time at the factory. BOB SHERWOOD, EXPORT MANAGER AT Chicago Dynamic Ind., received a cable from the Master of the Soviet ship Mikhail Lermontov, inquiring about the possibility of securing a Chi Coin "Holiday" ball bowler for placement in the ship's recreation area. Arrangements have not been confirmed, as yet. The ship is on its maiden voyage to the U. S., in the hopes of wooing the tourist trade, and is expected to dock in New York around June 11 ...ChiCoin's Avron Gensburg departed for Europe last week on a routine visit to the factory's distribs, reps, et al. UNDERSTAND FROM UNITED ARTISTS RECORDS' local representative Walter Paas that operators in the area have been showing a great deal of interest in the new single by Lou Donaldson called "Black Byrd." "MONTE CARLO" AND "ODDS & EVENS" continue to be the biggest sellers of the day at Bally Mfg. Co.-and there's no let-up in sight, according to Herb Jones! WITH THE COMPLETION, LAST WEEK, of sample shipments of the new single player "Gulfstream" by Williams Electronics Inc., factory distribs are now display- ing (and selling) the new piece-in a big way, according to Bill DeSelm! Bill also mentioned that "Paddle Ball," the video ping pong game, and "Golden Triangle," the new shuffle, are presently being shipped-in quantity! ON THE SINGLES SCENE: Gus Tartol of Singers One Stop notes that the following are among current releases being programmed by area operators: "Hey Mama" by Al Martino (Capitol), "Hurt" by Bobby Vinton (Epic), "Satin Sheets" by Jeanne Pruett (MCA), "Monster Mash" by Bobby Boris Pickett (Parrot) and "Kodachrome" by Paul Simon (Columbia). MILWAUKEE MENTIONS Jack Hastings of Hastings Dist. Inc. will be scheduling a Rock -Ola service school just as soon as a date can be confirmed with Rock -Ola engineer Bill Findlay. Meanwhile, the Rock -Ola phono models are selling like crazy out there! Jack's also enjoying steady sales activity on the Valley pool tables line. Although the Frigidaire ice machine is an all year around seller at Hastings, the expected surge at this time of the year is already being felt. HOPE ALL IS TIP TOP WITH Marie Pierce of Pierce Music in Broadhead. She's had some problems with a leg ailment and was scheduled to undergo corrective surgery-but not before all of her work was completed! CHATTED WITH STU GLASSMAN of Radio Doctors on one of his favorite subjects, that of how to better serve operators! "The importance of the operator must be recognized," he said, "considering the fact that operator purchases account for about one half of the total 45 record sales! We feel very strongly about this at Radio Doctors and frequently institute additional service tech- niques, geared specifically to our operator customers, to provide speedy and efficient handling of their orders" . . . As for some of the current items being programmed by area ops, John Jankowski, the expert in that department, noticed that more and more ops are putting rock and soft rock singles into their easy listening programming formats. This past week John has sold a lot of the new Deep Purple single "Smoke On The Water". Also, "Last Tango In Paris" by 101 Strings w/Bebe Bardon, "Send Me No Roses" by Tommy Overstreet and - "Daisy May And Daisy May Not" by Terri Lane. Also selling steadily are the oldies of '55 thru '65 vintage. Cash Box/R(iB News Report Clarence Lawton Joins Stereo Dim. VEW YORK - Loren Becker, pres- ident of Stereo Dimension, has an- iounced that Clarence Lawton, veteran R & B producer and promo- tional director, has joined the Stereo Dimension staff on an exclusory ba- sis. The agreement was finalized in New York, and became effective as of June 1st. Lawton had, up until this agree - (L. to R.) Loren Becker, Clarence Lawton and Fred Edwards. Music Bank Seeks `Oldies' Acts Music Bank Productions has an- nounced that Johnnie Richardson, fa- mous for her hits of "Over the Moun- tain, Across the Sea" as half of Johnnie & Joe and "Sally go Round The Roses" as the Jaynettes has just completed recording several new sides for her forthcoming album under the direction of Producer, Jay Warner. Warner also wrote, arranged and en- gineered the sessions. Warner has previously recorded The 5 Satins, Life U.S.A. Paul Carney, (Son of comedi- an Art Carney) and Dave Chester (whose 2nd record will be out on Babylon records in June) for Music Bank Productions. Jay Warner is cur- rently working on a co -production deal with Wilbert Harrison. Har- rison recorded the rock classic "Kansas City" and more recently had a hit with "Let's Work Together." Warner is currently looking for new and Oldie acts and can be reached at (212) 675-5167 (Shown above-L. to R.) Johnnie Richardson and producer Jay Warner. Frederick Knight Produces GSF's Lloyd Price ATLANTA, GA.-Stax recording art- ist Frederick Knight has been signed to produce a single on GSF label artist Lloyd Price for Bill Lowery Productions, a part of Lowery Group. The sessions will begin immediately at the Lowery Studio here with a rush release planned by the label. Although a mixture of songs from various writers will be used, the pri- mary emphasis will be given to new material from the Knight -Price writ- ing combine. During 15 years of success, Price has charted with "Stagger Lee", "Per- sonality," "(Johnny You're Too Young But) I'm Gonna Get Married," among many other hits. ment, a distribution deal with Stereo Dimension concerning his Master Five label, in conjunction with artists Baby Washington and Don Gardner, whose initial release, "Forever" is rapidly moving up all R & B charts. As per the recent commitment, Lawton will be involved in the sign- ing and development of new talent, the acquisition of masters, and will direct all promotional efforts in the R & B field. This incorporates two previ- ously established Stereo Dimension distributed R & B labels, Master Five and Fred Frank's Roadshow Records, and a new in-house R & B label, to be initiated later this month. Two strong R & B artists have already been signed to this debut label. Lawton's extensive background in the R & B field includes, most recent- ly, his affiliation with Avco Records, where he played a major role in bringing producer Thom Bell and the Stylistics to the label, as well as his strong promotional efforts on such Stylistics hits as "You Are Every- thing" and "Betch By Golly Wow," and other of the label's R & B suc- cesses. Previous to that he had his own label, Rare Bullet, and several publishing firms and his own indepen- dent production and promotion com- panies. To his credits Lawton has been associated with over fifty major R & B chart records. Becker feels, "This deal signifies that Stereo Dimension is making ma- jor long-range moves to firmly estab- lish its labels and its growing roster of artists in the R & B field." Warners Launches 'Soul Showcase BURBANK - David Banks, newly appointed director of special projects, r&b music, for Warner Bros. Records, announces the launching of a WB "Soul Showcase" campaign on a na- tional level to expose more widely the efforts of r&b artists on the label and to build the identity of Warner Bros. as a heavy contender in the r&b mar- ket. The "Soul Showcase" campaign will center around album and single product by WB artists including Tow- er of Power, Dionne Warwicke, Paul Kelly, Cold Blood, Malo and Maxayn, and singles by Bobby Sheen, the Hyp- notics, Bobby Byrd, the Classic Sul- livans and Spyder Turner. In the next few months, window and in-store displays, contests for lo- cal promotion teams and branch salesmen, special awards to radio sta- tions and personnel as well as buyers, and merchandising materials includ- ing the "Soul Bunny" poster, "Soul Bunny" necklace, "Soul Bunny" plaque and "Soul Bunny" T-Shirt will be utilized by Banks in the campaign. The "Soul Showcase" will be visual- ized through advertising, promotion, publicity and merchandising efforts by the company. David Banks, newly appointed direc- tor of special projects, R & B music, displays the first "Soul Bunny" poster to be used in the Warner Bros. "Soul Showcase" campaign. R I3 B INGREDIENTS-Bremar Services, Inc., (headed by Barry Gib- son, Don Sainte-Johnn and Wil Johnsen), based in Chicago, have one of the first and only nationally synicated three-hour weekly soul music count down shows, "Black 40". The show has been in production since the beginning of the year, and the acceptance is broadening. KALO of Little Rock and KOWH in Omaha, have recently bought the show and listener response has been excel- lent. "B-40" is also adaptable to top -40 radio according to Sainte-Johnn, WGRT- Chicago morning air personality, who hosts "Black 40". Weekly interviews are featured with artists who have current records on national charts. ("B-40" plays from the charts of a national publication). The show runs 45 -minutes, leaving 15 -minutes for station time (CA's, etc.). The show is offered on an exclusive market basis, according to company spokesmen ... Curtis Mayfield's new album release. "Back To The World", has a cut entitled, "Keep On Trip - pin' ", and the tune came through purely by accident. While guitarist -producer Phil Upchurch; bassist Lucky Scott and drummer Quentin Joseph were foolin' around during a studio session, Curtis overhead the impromptu session. He taped it, penned some lyrics and dubbed it, "Keep On Trippin' " and it is a standout track on the LP ... Also, from Curtom, a major publicity campaign, which may include a 10 -city tour, is being mapped out for Curtom artist LeRoy Hutson in conjunction with the release of his current album "Love Oh Love" . Bandleader Willie Colon (Fania) was the victim of a kidnap attack on a re- cent Saturday morning in New York. He fought of his attackers and he is now at Montifiore Hospital recuperating from a fractured nose and multiple frac- tures. But, come what may Colon will be back with his fans shortly . Half Note patrons, throughout the years, will be saddened to learn that William Alberg, better known as "Al the Waiter" died of a heart attack on May 7th in his apartment in NYC. Sonny and Mike Canterino, owners of the West 54th Street Jazz Club, found the body in his apartment late that night when the reliable longtime employee did not show up for work. Alberg, 58, was known throughout the jazz community for his warm sense of humour and for his rapid and patented manner of lighting patrons' cigarettes. cash twìr/ album Heuas LEON LIVE-Leon Russell-Shelter STCO- 8917 When talking of superstars, the name Leon Russell is an automatic addition to the roster. The man in concert is simply the most electric performer around in all of pop today. This three record live collection is the perfect indi- cation of Leon live and will be a massive success as a result. All of the electricity, the vibrancy, the moods and the feelings are in evidence and with material the likes of "Roll Away The Stone," "Crystal Closet Queen," "Delta Lady" and "Prince of Peace," this dy- namic set looks to be his most successful to date. THE FREE ELECTRIC BAND-Albert Hammond -Mums KZ -32267 The latest weather report from Albert is finally here and the forecast is for hits, hits, hits. This collection spearheaded by his current smash single, title track of this LP further demonstrates the diverse' talents of the man and further solidifies his pop super -standing. Possible singles are in abundance with "Re- becca", "The Day The British Army Lost The War" and "Smokey Factory Blues" leading in that direction. From the way things look at present, it never rains anywhere near Albert Hammond and quite possibly, never will. A true hitmaker of the seventies. FACTS OF LIFE-Bobby Womack-United Ar- tists-UA-LA043-F Bobby Womack has truly become an r&b super performer and it seems time for him to do the same magic in pop markets. Hot on the heels of his highly successful "Across 110th Street" soundtrack, Bobby has come up with a fine collection of winning tunes and some equally fine covers of pop tunes. Lead- ing off is the current single release "Nobody Wants You When You're Down And Out," a true powerhouse headed for the top, but "The Look Of Love," "Natural Man" and "All Along The Watchtower" are equal to the task and show great promise for the future. Look for this collection to finaly put Bobby Womack on the pop map, and in a prominent position, too. SUBWAY SERENADE-Looking Glass-Epic- KE 32167 The- "Brandy" bunch is back with another solid collection of pop tunes that should do much to further and enhance their pop career. In delivering a grouping of tunes ranging from the softest of ballad to the rockingest of rock, the group again displays their talents and offers a fine group of single possibilities. Lead- ing the way is "Jimmy Loves Mary Anne," the groups latest hit, but listen closely to the rocking "Sweet Jeremiah" and the steady "Wooly Eyes." This is one Looking Glass that is reflecting many future successes. O LUCKY MAN - Original Soundtrack - Alan Price-Warner Brothers-BS 2710 Alan Price, the same of the Animals and the Alan Price Set, dynamically re -appears of the recording scene with this perfect soundtrack for the latest Malcolm McDowell -Lindsay An- derson film. Price melodically combines pop and folk rock in creating a solid total album of music. The single is the title track, but "Poor People," "Look Over Your Shoulder" and "Changes" could just as easily succeed. O how lucky we all are to have Alan back and record- ing again. Don't pass this one up. POP PICKS SOUNDTRACK PICKS LOVE DEVOTION SURRENDER-Carlos San- tana & Mahavishnu John McLoughlin- Columbia KC -32034 In what is definitely a progessive music followers delight, Santana and McLoughlin, two of today's leading guitarists, have put their talents to the test and have come up with a tremendous winning collection of prog- ressively minded jazz-rock material guaranteed to mesmerize even the most non-musical ear. Although each track is excellent in it's own right, "Let Us Go Into The House of The Lord" and "A Love Supreme" stand magnificently above the rest. Definitely a brilliant collection and worthy of anyone's collection. NEWCOMER PICKS FRESH-Sly and the Family Stone-Epic-KE 32134 This long awaited disk from the long absent Sly and his Family Stone proves conclusively that Sly has been up to only good. This album is possibly the strongest the group has ever released and, as a result, should be their most successful. Absolutely immaculate production combined with the group's overwhelming musi- cal talent makes this "fresh" collection of material an absolute gold mine for hits. The current single, "If You Want Me To Stay" was the natural, but listen to "In Time", "I Don't Know (Satisfaction)", "Keep On Dancin' " and "Que Sera Sera (Whatever Will Be. Will Be)" to decide on the follow up. Here's hoping that "Fresh" means a fresh, new start for Sly, a perrenial rock and roll powerhouse. CROSSWORD PUZZLE-The Partridge Family -Bell 1122 Not a difficult one to figure out, this one is going straight to the top and should be the beginning of another string of Partridge hits. Leading the pack is what must be the single, "One Day At A Time", a solid, harmonious pop vehicle that just won't be stopped in it's journey to the top of the singles charts. As usual David Cassidy shines and Shirley Jones fills the background with sweet vocals. Once again, the proper spelling is s -u -c -c -e -s -s. MY MERRY-GO-ROUND-Johnny Nash-Epic KE 32158 Johnny is hot and ready to "steer" up loads of action with this his latest LP. On the heels of his chart busting "I Can See Clearly Now" and "Stir It Up" singles, comes this power packed collection guaranteed to solidify his popular standing. Although Johnny's style of late has been reggae, this collection touches many bases and shows the diverse talents of the performer. "You Better Stop (Messing Around)", a stunning Otis Redding -like blues - soul piece and "My Merry -Go -Round" are best examples. More and more Look for '73 to be- come Johnny's year as time goes by. LANCASHIRE HUSTLER - Keef Hartley - Deram XDES-18070 It's taken some time but it looks as if the time has come for Keef Hartley to be "dis- covered" by the world. This latest LP should be the vehicle with which to accomplish that feat. In taking a page from h.s blues text, Keef has come up with nine solid tracks of pure British musical entertainment. "Dance To The Music", an extended six minute ver- sion, would seem a likely single release, but don't discount an edited version of "Action". Look for lots more "hustle" from this pro- gressively minded Briton in the future. The initial "noise" has finally been made. SUPER FLY T.N.T.-Osibisa-Original Sound- track-Buddah-BDS 5136 ST Osibisa once again criss crosses their Afri- can rhythms, this time in the form of the soundtrack for the latest "Superfly" extrava- ganza. Heated performances should do as much for this follow up flick as Curtis Mayfield did for the original. Highlights, and singles are everywhere, but the title track is definitely the top contender. Infectious quality of the re- cording will do much for this previously under- rated band. Solid from start to finish. ROGER MC GUINN-Columbia KC -31946 In his first solo effort since dissolving the Byrds, Roger has compiled and performs a ton of solid material definitely heavy enough to launch his new career. Although his voice will always be fondly looked upon as that lead voice of the Byrds, this new identity finds him as a totally individual performer strong enough to stand on it's own and develop it's own individuality. Powerhouse tracks are, naturally, everywhere but "Lost My Driving Wheel," "My New Woman" and "Draggin' " seem to have the greatest single possibilities. Look for this new McGuinn career to be a tremendously successful venture. Cash Box -June 23, 1973 35 www.americanradiohistory.com

GRC Signs Producer, 9 Artists ATLANTA - Michael Thevis, pres- ident of the General Record Corpora- tion (GRC), a Michael Thevis Enter- prise, recently signed Mike Terry as staff arranger and producer for the company's two recording labels: GRC and AWARE. The young musician has arranged and played for more than five mil- lion -selling records and was em- ployed by both Motown and Golden World studios. NEW ACTS GRC has also announced a series of contract signings with nine artists and groups. These include writer/singer Sammy Johns; writer/producer Floyd Smith; singers Danny Johnson and John Ed- wards; singer Marlys Roe; progres- sive soul group Ripple; country/light rock group Heartwood; coun- try/bluegrass group Red, White and Blue (grass), and the group Homegrown, contemporary pop art- ists. Sammy Johns, a gospel and light pop performing artist, has just com- pleted recording his first single, "Shake A Hand", which will .be re- leased June 6 on the GRC label. Floyd Smith, who is among the first of what will be a number of well recognized talents to become involved in Atlanta's growing music scene, has a long list of credentials and suc- cesses in the music business, both as a writer and a producer. He recently produced Loleatta Holloway's re- cording, "Mother of Shame", which was released May 14 on the AWARE Adelphi Inks Gerry Goff in For Disk Dates NEW YORK - Adelphi Records is pleased to announce the signing of Gerry Goffin, whose past composer credits include hits in collaboration with Carole King, Barry Mann and others. The music produced in association with Adelphi Records will be Gerry's first exposure as a featured vocalist; the songs were co-authored with Bar- ry Goldberg. Adelphi will be releasing immedi- ately two singles drawn from Ger- ry's forthcoming album: "Maryland Again" b/w "It's Not the Spotlight" and "Tojo Saloon" b/w "Down on the Street". The album, which will be a two -disc package, will be ready for release in late July and will be entitled "It Ain't Exactly Entertainment". Session musicians for the songs in- clude Barry Goldberg, Eddie Hinton, Jesse "Pete" Carr, Paul Hornsby, Jerry Masters, Jeanie Green and the Muscle Shoals Horns. Goffin produced the sessions. IT'S ALL SMILES at the Califor- nia offices of A. Schroeder Interna- tional Ltd. where Gary Le Mel (seated), newly appointed director of creative services west, writer -artist - producer Barry White, and Aaron and Abby Schroeder recently cel- ebrated Barry's smash single "I'm Gonna Love You Just A Little More Baby" and his hot album "I've Got So Much To Give". label (GRC). At age 17, Smith's com- position, "When You're Alone", rec- orded by the Hilltoppers, was a na- tional top ten smash hit. John Edwards and Danny Johnson, both natives of Chicago, were discov- ered within a few weeks of one an- other in their hometown of Chicago by GRC producer Floyd Smith. Ed- wards has just recorded his first sin- gle "Merry Go Round", produced by Floyd Smith at the Atlanta firm's Sound Pit studio. This single will be released July 16. Johnson, a light pop singer, will be recording his first single for release also in July. Marlys -Roe a young performer with two previous records published to her credit during college, has been entertaining as a solo artist in lead- ing clubs in Nashville for the past three years. Marlys enjoys singing all types of music including classical, pop and her favorite style-country. The Ripple artists include Michigan natives Dave Ferguson, Keith Sa- muels, Brian Sherrer, Curtis Rey- nolds, Walter Carter, Ken Carter and Bill Hull. The group's first single re- lease. recorded at GRC's new studio, the Sound Pit, is entitled "I Don't Know What It Is But It Sure Is Funky". Combining the talents of Tim Hil- debrandt as guitarist and songwriter, Robert Hudson on drums and guitar, Joe McGlohan playing steel guitar, Bryon Paul on bass, and Gary John- son also on bass, Heartwood will be recording their first album, contain- ing 11 of their original songs, for release in mid-August. Members of Red, White and Blue (Grass) consist of Norman Blake, reknown guitarist and mandolin mu- sician who has appeared with Johnny Cash in several concert appearances; Grant Boatright on lead guitar, Dave Sebolt on bass, Dale Whitcomb on banjo and fiddle and Ginger Boatright on guitar and vocals. Group will be recording their first album for release in late August. Homegrown, a four -man contem- porary recording group, consists of Bobby Tate on guitar and vocals, Barry Abernathy on bass; G. C. Cole- man on percussion and Steve Carey on keyboard and harmonica. Each art- ist had worked as professional back- up musicians for artists including Johnny Mathis, Buddy Hackett, Andy Williams, Bobby Darin, Otis Redding and Curtis Mayfield. Farrell, Dumon To Admn Ben Pub HOLLYWOOD - The Wes Farrell Organization, in association with the Damont Corporation, has entered into an agreement to exclusively ad- minister the publishing firm of Blen Music on a worldwide basis, ac- cording to David Mook, managing director of WFO on the west coast. The agreement was finalized by Ben Weisman, head of Blen Music, and David Mook on behalf of Da - mont and the Wes Farrell Organiza- tion. The publishing firm controls the rights to such Weisman compositions as "The Night Has a Thousand Eyes," recently revitalized by The Carpenters on their new album, the title song from Andy Warhol's "L'A- mour" recorded by Cass Elliot, and the movie themes "Where Did I Go Wrong" and "The Young Ameri- cans," both written by Weisman with Academy -Award -winner Paul Francis Webster. In his composing career, Weisman has written 57 songs that heve been recorded by Elvis Presley. DOUBLE FIRST-Jay Lasker, president of ABC/Dunhill Records, has an- nounced the signing of Albert Brooks to the label. The event marks a couple of "firsts" for both the company and the artist. Brooks is the first comedian to record for ABC/Dunhill. When he appears at the Troubadour in Los Angeles from July 3rd to the 8th, Brooks will be the only performer to ever play the club without first recording an album. Seated is Jay Lasker with (standing 1-r) Herb Nanas, Brooks' manager; Mary Helfer, vice president at ABC/Dun- hill in charge of artist relations; and Albert Brooks. British Group Signed To Stax NEW YORK - Marking a signifi- cant expansion in its list of artists, Stax Records has signed the British rock group Skin Alley to the label, giving the group its first exposure to the American market. Coincident with signing the group, Stax has released its first American album, "Two Quid Deal," featuring original compositions by members of the group. Featured in the group are Tony Knight, drums, former leader of Tony Knight's Chessmen; Nick Gra- ham, vocals, bass piano, flute, formerly of Atomic Rooster; Krystof Juskiewicz, keyboards, formerly of the Pendulum, and Bob James, gui- tar, vocals, flute, alto and soprano sax, of The Shadows. Stax is presently preparing an American tour for Skin Alley. Sea Cruise Is Jimmy Payne Rep ST. LOUIS - Writer -singer - musician Jimmy Payne has reached an agreement for management rep- resentation by Ken Keene, president of Sea Cruise Productions. Payne is the co -writer of "Woman, Woman," the first million seller for Gary Puckett & The Union Gap. He has songs recorded by John David- son, Robert Goulet, The Lettermen, Rav Price, Tammy Wynette, The Ed Sullivan Orchestra, Rich Landers, Bill Anderson, Del Reeves, Jeanne Pruett, among others. J. Payne is a recording artist for Vanguard Records in New York. His current release is "Sold American." Previous chart records include "Western Union Wire," "L. A. An- gels," and "Woman, Woman". For information of bookings, rec- ords, etc., contact Ken Keene, Sea Cruise Productions, P. 0. Box 11387, St. Louis, Missouri 63105. Cash Box/MIB News Report NAIRA Meets Aug. 8 In New Orleans CLEVELAND - NATRA's pres- ident, Curtis Shaw of Cleveland, has announced that he intends to seek a second term as head of that organi- zation. In announcing his intentions, Shaw said, "it is my belief that an incum- bent President must seek reelection on the record he established while in office." Shaw then proceeded to out- line ten points of accomplishment within the past two years including the recently adopted Constitution and Code of Regulations, the Summer In- stitute Seminars, special services to the membership, and financial matur- ity. Shaw, who has provided a uniquely different style of leadership for NA - TRA, says that, "the first two years were extremely challenging and have set the stage and pace for many great things in the next couple of years." When asked to elaborate on plans for NATRA in the next two years Shaw declined saying that, "I don't have any announced opposition and would prefer to deal with spe- cifics at a later date." Shaw did say however that work has begun on in- novative programs for NATRA which will be announced at or before Convention '73 in New Orleans, Louisiana. When asked if he thought he would have any opposition Shaw replied, "Probably. There is always someone that wants to be President because they think it's glamorous. They real- ly have no idea how much work and time is involved in the mere day to day business of an association this size." Shaw went on to say how he hopes the membership will recognize the dedication he has to the job and that will retain him. NATRA's Convention '73 will be August 8-12 at the Marriott Hotel in New Orleans, Louisiana. Show Stopping Gold STYLISTICS FIRST-During their recent headline engagement at the Copa- cabana, the Stylistics were presented with their first million -dollar album from Avco Records. Luigi Creatore, vice president of Avco, made the presentation on opening night with a gold disc for the group's debut LP, "The- Stylistics". While they were in New York, The Stylistics, also donated their services to the "Cavalcade Of Stars", a charity show for retarded children at Madison Square Garden on June 7. Seen above (1 to r): Airrion Love, James Smith, James Dunn, Herb Murrell and Russell Thompkins, Jr. of the Stylistics with Luigi Creatore. Medgar Evers Tribute Day MISSISSIPPI HOMECOMING. William Bell, Dick Gregory, B. B. King, Mrs. Medgar Evers and Rev. Cleophus Robinson were among those who answered Fayette (Miss.) Mayor Charles Evers' call to a "Mississippi Homecoming" by participating in the all -day Medgar Evers Memorial Festival held June 12. The event brought thousands of people to Fayette for a morning memorial service, a parade, a picnic with local entertainment and a big 6 hour evening show in the Jackson Coliseum with B. B. King, the Staple Singers, Rev. Cleophus Robinson, Dick Gregory, Willie Dixon, James Earl Jones, Robert Earl Jones, William Bell, Little Milton and Eddie Floyd. R i. B INGREDIENTS-James Baldwin has scripted an account of Ray Charles life. "The Hallelujah Chorus: The Life and Times of Ray Charles" depicts the story of Ray Charles' struggle with his music, blindness, drugs and his own genius. In a dramatic and musical form, the Baldwin theatrical concert is to be presented July 1 at Carnegie Hall, in NYC. The master of Rhythm and Blues will also perform in the work. James Baldwin, as narrator, and Ray Charles have long admired each other's work, but this is the first creative meeting of these two artists. Cicely Tyson, Academy Award nominee for her role in, "Sounder" will take part in a bare stage dramatization which will relate some of the elements that compose the psychological develment of black art- ists like Ray Charles. The concert salute should be a moving experience for both the audience and the performers ... Soul Brother Number One James Brown has completed work on the motion picture score for "Slaughter's Big Rip -Off", an AIP film starring Jim Brown. The film premieres July 3 at the Fox Theatre in Detroit. The new Polydor LP, scored by Brown with Fred Wesley, also features the JBs and Lyn Collins, whose single "How Long Can I Keep It Up" is now in release on the People label . Atlantic Records, recognizing the tremendous talents of The Spinners as a recording and performing group, toasted their latest Gold Record winners in a party held at the Park Lane Hotel, in NYC. A jam packed throng of press and industry personnel stopped by to honor and rap with the personable group. There was plenty of food and good cheer to partake of. And, in an adage that seems most appropo, 'if you got it flaunt it' and enjoy it while you can. This group, around for some twenty years, has paid its dues. When the public goes out and purchases the product that you deliver to the extent that warrants a gold record, how can one hesitate to say that they deserve it. In so many industries, a loyal employee, who has spent 25 years with a firm, is rewarded with a dinner, a pat on the back, and a gold watch; then is sent out to pasture to tick off the time ... Jerry Bolding, program consultant at WOOK in Washington made the following statement in reply to an article that appeared in the Wall Street Journal, June 19th. "I was misquoted and misinterpreted in the article which appeared in Tuesday, July 19 Wall Street Journal (by Jonathan Kwitny). It has been my contention that if a scandal situation does exist in the music industry, it certainly must involve more than just blacks. My primary concern is based on the fact that everytime the word 'payola' emerges, blacks are always the culprits and I feel this is wrong." The above is the actual statement by Jerry. don drossell Over 70 Jazz Artists to Honor Louis Armstrong On July 4th NEW YORK - The City of New York in tribute to Louis Armstrong is changing the name of the Singer Bowl to Louis Armstrong Stadium. Over 70 major jazz personalities will pay homage to Louis on his birth- day, July 4th. The musical jamboree is part of the Newport Jazz Festival - New York and will be one of the largest jazz tributes ever presented. Among those appearing at the out- door stadium will be comedian George Kirby and an incredible list of jazz giants which include among others: Count Basie, Eubie Blake, Dave Brubeck, Cab Calloway, Cozy Cole, Eddie Lockjaw Davis, Wild Bill Davison, Drootin Brothers, Roy El - ridge, Ella Fitzgerald, Stan Getz, Dizzy Gillespie, Tyree Glenn, Al Grey, Tiny Grimes, Earl Hines, Fred- die Hubbard, Helen Humes, Elvin Jones, Gene Krupa, Ellis Larkins, Yank Lawson, Howard McGhee, John Mayall, Turk Murphy, Joe Newman, Anita O'Day, Jimmy Owens, Sam Rivers, Archie Shepp, James Spauld- ing, Sun Ra, Billy Taylor, Clark Ter- ry, Sarah Vaughan, Eddie Cleanhead Wilber, Cootie Williams, Joe Williams, Reginald Workman, and many others will be announced. The jazz jamboree will start at 1:00 P. M. and all seats are priced at $5.00. For further information for this and all Festival events, write Newport Jazz Festival -New York, P. O.
