SHORTER S BETTER. In advertising as in music, Shorter Is Better, so let us merely say that: -Mr.Wayne Shorter, the dazzling saxophone virtuoso of Weather Report fame, has made a solo album called "Native Dancer..." And Mr. Milton Nascimento, the great Brazilian composer and guitarist, has joined Mr. Shorter in creating an entirely new sound-soft ( Brazilian), phenomenally rhythmic (African maybe), and sensationally full of energy (American)... And Mr. Herbie Hancock, the pianist, is here too, along with some more of the best musicians alive... And the result is simply one of the most beautiful records we have ever heard. Enjoy it. Wayne Shorter. www.americanradiohistory.com
===== PAGE 10 =====
cash box,- news Talbert Named Arista R&B Product Chief NEW YORK - Clive Davis. president of Arista Records, announced last week the appointment of Hank Talbert to the new- ly created post of national director of r&b product. Talbert, whose responsibilities will be wide ranging from r&b artist ac- quisition and development through pro- motion and merchandising of r&b prod- uct will report directly to Elliot Goldman, Arista's executive vice president. Talbert's immediate duties will encom- pass the supervision of r&b promotion and the hiring and direction of the r&b promotion staff as well as the initial formulation of merchandising and marketing plans for r&b product. In addi- tion, he will work closely with Davis in the evaluation of masters and artists in the r&b area. Talbert comes to Arista from Buddah Records where he served as vice presi- dent in charge of the r&b division. Prior to that Talbert served as general manager of operations and national director of promotion and sales for Hot Wax and Music Merchant, divisions of Holland, Dozier, and Holland. Talbert Ted Feigin Forms Prod. -Mgt. Company NEW YORK - Ted Feigin, a veteran of the record industry, last week an- nounced that he has formed a new pro- duction -management -publishing com- pany called Ted Feigin Associates. He will operate out of offices on both the east and west coasts. The New York of- fice will be located at 444 East 82 St. The Los Angeles address is 1440 Veteran Ave. Feigin was president of White Whale Records that hit with the Turtles some years ago. More recently he was assis- tant to the president, Clive Davis, when Davis was head of Columbia. He played a key role in the signing of a number of artists to Columbia. He last held the post of vp of a&r, west coast operations at CBS. Feigin expects to be announcing the signing of a number of key acts to his operation shortly. John Rosica Leaves ABC HOLLYWOOD - Cash Box has learned that John Rosica, vice-president, market- ing of ABC Records, has left the label to pursue outside interests. Rosica, who joined ABC in August 1974 as vice- president and general manager of the ABC/Impulse label and as ABC east coast office head, will announce his future plans shortly. Price Named MCA Vice Pres. NEW YORK - Frank Price, president of Universal Television, has been named a vice president of the parent company, MCA Inc., it was reported last week by Sidney J. Sheinberg, president and chief operating officerof MCA Inc. Price joined Universal Television as associate producer and writer in 1959, subsequently becoming executive pro- ducer of a number of television series in- cluding "The Virginian," "Ironside," "It Takes A Thief" and several "World Premiere Movies." He was named a vice president of Universal Television in 1964, senior vice president in 1971 and president in July 1974. Torres Joins Buddah Group NEW YORK - Fred Ruppert national director of promotion at Buddah Records, has announced that Bernie Torres has been named to handle na- tional singles promotion for the label. Torres will work out of the Los Angeles office of Buddah Records. Torres joins Buddah Records after fif- teen years as executive assistant to Bill Drake. A graduate of the University of San Francisco, Torres was involved with the creation of the Drake Programming System which is best known for its trendsetting work with the RKO chain of stations and most recently, K100 in Los Angeles. Wardell To Head London Creative Services Dept. NEW YORK - Don Wardell has been ap- pointed to the position of director of creative services at London Records. Wardell's department will be responsi- ble for all radio, television and print ad- vertising for artist relations, in-store dis- plays and special marketing campaigns. He will report to Herb Goldfarb, the vice president of sales and marketing. Radio promotion will now be directed by Walt Maguire vice president of a&r. Wardell Wasserman New Stones PR Rep BEVERLY HILLS - The Rolling Stones and Sunday Promotions have hired Paul Wasserman, executive vice-president of Jim Mahoney and Associates, to be their exclusive press and public relations representative for North and South America. Wasserman, who headquarters in Los Angeles, was in New York week of Apr. 28 to coordinate a planned May 1 press conference in which various Stones' pro- jects and activities through the re- mainder of the year will be revealed. Naha, Ring Named To CBS Posts NEW YORK Mickey Eichner, vice pre- sident of east coast a&r for Columbia Records, has disclosed the appointment of Ed Naha to the position of associate producer of Columbia a&r on the east coast. Naha will be responsible for coordinat- ing various a&r projects on the east coast, including the acquisition of new talent, as well as creating a new, periodical Columbia a&r newsletter. Naha first joined Columbia Records in Sept. 1972 in the position of publicity writer. After moving up to east coast press representative, he was promoted to manager of east coast press and public information, a position he has held until this new move. Additionally, Bob Altshuler, vice presi- dent of press and public information for the CBS Records group, has reported the appointment of Sherry Ring to the position of admistrator of press and public information. Ms. Ring will be responsible for assist- ing in various administrative functions, including the maintenance of the Colum- bia, Epic and CBS Custom label budgets for the press and public information de- partment and the planning of press parties and concert arrangements. She will also become involved in various publicity projects. She will report direct- ly to Judy Paynter and Bob Sarlin, the directors of press and public information. Williams New UA Art Head LOS ANGELES - Bob Cato, vice presi- dent, creative services, United Artists Records, has announced the appoint- ment of Thom Williams to the post of art director, trade and consumer advertising for all UA and Blue Note artists. Prior to joining UA, Williams had been a free lance art director on projects for Warner Brothers Music, Paramount Records, Motown Records, ABC Records, 20th Century Records and various other music industry companies. He had also been creative director for the Electric Circus Company for five years. Williams has been the recipient of several awards from the Art Directors Clubs of New York and Los Angeles; the Society of Illustrators; the American Institute of Graphic Arts and the Type Directors Club. His television com- mercials for Motown earned him medals from the Atlanta International Film Festival in 1973 and 1974. He was also awarded a Clio in the radio commercial category in 1969. Williams' graphic work has been featured in such magazines as Art Direc- tor, Consumer Arts and Industrial Design. A graduate of New York's Pratt Institute, Williams is headquartered in Los Angeles and reports directly to Cato. Williams Lott To Direct R&B At Buddah NEW YORK - Art Kass, president of The Buddah Group, announced last week that Alan Lott has been appointed na- tional director of r&b operations. Lott will be responsible for promotion, merchandising, and artist development of the company's roster. He will also play a major roll in Buddah's a&r develop- ment and overall involvement in black culture. He will report directly to Art Kass. Prior to this appointment, Lott was, for two years, national promotion director of album product of Atlantic/Atco Records. While at Atlantic he was instrumental in the development of the careers of the Spinners, Blue Magic, Major Harris, Billy Cobham, Stanley Clarke, and the Average White Band. Lott came to Atlantic/Atco from the WEA Cherry Hill, N.J. branch where he Lott Pell Set for Song Fest Directorship BEVERLY HILLS - Dave Pell has been named director of screening quality for the 1975 American Song Festival, an- nounced festival president Malcolm C. Klein. Pell served for eight years as chairman of the screening committee for the Los Angeles chapter of the Grammy Awards. His function was compartmentalizing nominated songs into the correct cate- gories. SASCO Combines East Coast, West Coast Concerns NEW YORK - Sid Seidenberg, presi- dent of Sidney A. Gloria Bell con- tinues to handle administration as Seid- enberg's executive assistant and Floyd Lieberman, vice president of S.A.S., will be coordinating publishing administra- tion and working more intensively in the management division. up front cash box, -'album reviews "Will the economic squeeze drive record produc- tion back to the labels' a&r departments and away from independent production?" Rupert Perry, General Manager, A&R, Capitol Records, Inc. The answer as far as Capitol Records is concerned, at this time, is no. We strongly believe in the independent producer, and our past experiences have proven highly successful. At the same time we do have our own in- house production. Dave Cavanaugh, John Palladino and John Carter all do in-house production for the label. We like to be able to marry artists that have signed or are signing with Capitol to a producer that they feel happy with and thus build a compatible and successful rela- tionship. It is very important that the artist be creatively happy. By utilizing independent producers along with the in-house person- nel, we are able to achieve this end. Certainly, Capitol wants the best pro- ducers for its artists which ultimately results in the best product. Don Ellis, Vice President, Columbia Records, West Coast Artists and Repertoire The choice of producer should never be dictated by economics. A successful producer/artist relationship is a delicate matter that is best founded on the interaction between the parties. While it is obvious that Columbia is moving strongly to re-establish an in-house production staff (i.e. Jack Gold's new record with Andy Williams and Joe Wissert's current involvement with Flo & Eddie) it is still our main objective to match artists and producers in a partnership that will succeed. To that degree we are utilizing the services of most of the current "name" pro- ducers and are also actively involved in giving an opportunity to some of the up and coming producers. Everyone involved in the artistic process at Columbia is well aware of economic pressures, but first and foremost it's always what is artistically correct that counts. Steve Barri, Vice President, A&R, ABC Records Frankly, I don't think the country's economic condi- tion has much to do with it. As we have in the past, we will always try to find the best producer possible for any act we are interested in recording - and, of course, we would prefer that he be from within the company. But if making the best record makes it necessary for us to spend a little more money and hire an outside produc- tion company, then we'll do it. And surprisingly, despite the economic squeeze, more completed masters are be- ing offered to us now than ever before. Mike Berniker, Director of Popular Artists & Repertoire, RCA Records I don't believe that the economic squeeze will drive record production back into what once was considered the in-house a&r staff concept. What we have at RCA Records instead is a mix of the two, whereby we're now making active choices of who will produce new artists, as in the case of Paul Rothchild's producing Elliott Murphy, and in-house producers Mike Lipskin and myself producing Blue Mitchell, Cedar Walton, Jim Grady and Jack Jones. We are still deeply involved in the review and purchase of masters. And, in the past year, such reviews have resulted in the arrival of Reunion and Stark & McBrien. Our recent important signees, Hall & Oates and Aztec Two -Step, are in the process of being carefully assigned producers. While all of this is going on, there is no doubt that our policy has included, along with every other major label, the participation of production, distribution and label ar- rangements of a high order. These arrangements have resulted in the arrival at RCA Records of such artists as Carol Douglas, Leslie West, Lonnie Liston Smith and The Deadly Nightshade, among others. There is no question that the economic squeeze does not alter the fact that well -managed, creative independent labels have provided great profits for most of the major labels, and is a fact of the business that must be adhered to. Kip Cohen, Vice President, A&R, A&M Records Whereas current economics are undoubtedly prompt- ing labels to monitor recording costs more closely, in- sisting on adequate pre -recording rehearsels, etc., there is no reason to believe that "in-house" production is the exclusive solution. An artist belongs with the best possible producer each time he records, and the criterion for the selection of that man has nothing to do with whether or not he's an independent. jazz picks SILENT TONGUES - Cecil Taylor - Arista AL 1005 Quality of Performance outstanding Quality of Recording: good Style of Music: avante -garde; solo piano Comment: This record was recorded at Montreux in 1974, Taylor is one of the most impressive musicians performing anywhere in the world. One owes it to himself to listen to this disk. NATIVE DANCER - Wayne Shorter- Columbia PC 33418 Quality of Performance: good Quality of Recording: good Style of Music: small and large ensemble voicings. Comment: The music on this disk was composed by Shorter and Milton Nascimiento. Many of the Brazilian vocalist's pieces are based upon native folk themes. These ele- ments are sparked by their placement in a different, more European context. THE GIANT Dizzy Gillespie - Prestige P 24047 Quality of Performance: excellent Quality of Recording: excellent Style of Music: post -bop "Diz" with latin influences; small ensemble Comment: These tracks were made in Paris in April of 1973 and were released on the American label. This record will demonstrate why few trumpet players will ever be able to solo like Dizzy! With Kenny Clarke, Johnny Griffin and Niels Pedersen. PORTO NOVO - Marion Brown-Arista AL 1001 Quality of Performance: good Quality of Recording: good Style of Music: avant-garde Comment: This Freedom recording was made in Europe in 1967. It is as fresh today as it was then. One of the outstanding features of this LP is the quality of Brown's compositions. SPANISH BLUE - Ron Carter - CTI 6051 Quality of Performance: good Quality of Recording: excellent Style of Music: large ensemble, bass soloist Comment: This lush and serene LP integrates the traditional Spanish flamenco into a modern, improvisational format. A highlight is "Do What" from the historic Miles Davis "Kind Of Blue" session. CHICK COREA - Blue Note LA 395-H2 Quality of Performance: outstanding Quality of Recording: good Style of Music: the record develops Corea's art, from the mainstream to the abstract; small and large ensemble Comment: A collection of Corea's BN product from 1968 to 1970. The record serves as a fine primer for Corea's later Return to Forever work through its specification of Corea's roots. INTUITION Bill Evans - Fantasy F-9475 Quality of Performance: good Quality of Recording: good Style of Music: piano, bass duet Comment: Eddie Gomez joins Evans on this extremely coherent LP. Gomez and Evans have a sympathic understanding of each other's music. The product is quite in- tellectually stimulating. CONSCIOUSNESS - Pat Martino - Muse 5039 Quality of Performance: excellent Quality of Recording: good Style of Music: small ensemble, guitar solo; mainstream Comment: Martino's quartet is composed of Eddie Green, Tyrone Brown and Sherman Ferguson. Material like Coltran's "Impressions" and Eric Kloss' "Conscious- ness" serve as excellent vehicles for improvisation. These musicians are technical masters. BAD AND BEAUTIFUL - Sun Ra and His Arkestra - Impulse ASD 9276 Quality of Performance: good Quality of Recording: fair Style of Music: orchestral improvisation Comment: This record was originally released on the Saturn label in 1961. Surpris- ingly, the music is quite accessible; many of the more "outside" elements typical of the Arkestra are not employed. THE GREAT JAZZ ALBUM - Various Artists - Project 3 PR 2 6009 10 Quality of Performance: good Quality of Recording: outstanding Style of Music: big band (various styles, from swing to jazz-rock) Comment: Among the many artists appearing on this record are Louis Armstrong, Duke Ellington, Richard Davis and Larry Coryell. They perform standards like "A Train." "Satin Doll," "Stompin' At The Savoy" and "Sing, Sing, Sing." ATLANTIS - McCoy Tyner - Milestone M-55002 Quality of Performance: outstanding Quality of Recording: excellent Style of Music: small combo Comment: This two -record set was recorded live at The Keystone Korner in San Fran- cisco. Tyner is one of the world's great pianists and his "Atlantis" is a masterpiece. Catch the work of young Azar Lawrence on tenor and sop sax. 12 May 10, 1975 www.americanradiohistory.com

Ahmanson CTI Gemini Artists Show Set HOLLYWOOD - CTI Records will pre- sent "CTI Spring Jazz," a special concert highlighting ten top CTI artists, Sat., May 16, at L.A.'s Ahmanson Theater at 8:30 pm. The concert will feature CTI peren- nials Chet Baker, George Benson, Ron Carter, Hank Crawford, Joe Farrell, Bob James, Hubert Laws, Idris Muhammed, Johnny Hammond and Grover Washing- ton, Jr. Motown Records, which distributes CTI, will also coordinate itineraries and arrangements for the CTI artists, all of whom are being specially routed for the occasion. The label has planned a full program of support for the event. In addition to current releases by Bob James, Ron Carter, Joe Farrell and the Grover Washington, Jr., many of the participating artists will be debuting new releses, Hubert Laws' "Chicago Theme" is scheduled for release just prior to the concert. Ron Carter's new release, as of yet untitled, is tentatively scheduled for June. For the first time in its history, the label will release a single not contained in any previously released album. "Supership" features a vocal by George Benson and marks the vocal debut of the guitarist. Chet Baker is currently represented by "She Was Too Good To Me" and more recently teamed with Gerry Mulligan on a recorded Carnegie Hall series. Farrell, currently scoring with "Canned Funk." Label -sponsored performances and tours are an integral part of the CTI marketing strategy. In the early seven- ties, the label quietly pioneered the ap- proach with a concert at the Hollywood Palladium where the label's first in- dependently distributed release was re- corded. Subsequent tours included a midwest college tour, a performance at the summer olympics in 1972 and global performances in Japan, France, Van- couver and Hawaii. cash box, -'album reviews STAMPEDE - Doobie Bros. - Warner Bros. BS 2835 - Producer: Ted Templeman The latest offering from the Doobie Bros. is go- ing to come as a shock to those who felt themselves totally familiar with the band and their music. The music has taken on a symphonic quality that, when combined with this disk's de- cidedly root leanings, results in a surprising change of pace. Stampede can be summed up in one word - guitar. The distinctive axe styles of Tom Johnston, Pat Simmons and Jeff Baxter form a clear, distinctive balance to Johnston's one of a kind vocals to produce song successes like "Rainy Day Crossroad Blues" and "I Cheat The Hangman. The Doobies are one Stampede you won't want to get out of the way of. AIN'T LIFE GRAND - Black Oak Arkansas - At - co SD 36-111 - Producer: Richard Podolor Black Oak records all have one thing in com- mon. They're uniformally energetic, loud, raunchy and so greasy you can tube your car with one. Happily "Ain't Life Grand" continues in this vein. Once again the trademark of the band is Jim Mangrum's raspy vocals (which have been favorably likened to a rusty nail being dragged across a piece of glass) take apart and re- construct the likes of "Taxman" and "Good Stuff" while the band provides a bruising hardrock backing. Black Oak Arkansas is music to get hot and nasty by. USA - King Crimson - Atlantic SD 181 36 - Producer: King Crimson Over the years Robert Fripp s skills as a pro- gressive musician have been matched only by his ability to bring together equally skillful musical hands for the various incarnations of King Crimson. The abilities of both are shown in their finest light in USA. "Lark's Tongues In Aspic" and "21st Century Schizoid Man" reach their peak on this live disk as the totality of the musicianship of Crimson takes on added dimension and depth. USA is a little bit of musical madness in the night but it's insanity you're better off having. NEWBORN - James Gang - Atco SD 36-112 - Producer: Tom Dowd When Joe Walsh departed the consensus around the music world was that the James Gang would go the way of all rock and roll flesh. Their latest, "Newborn" points out that nothing could be further from the truth. The axe duo of Bubba Keith and Richard Shack are rock and roll weathermen; raining down riff upon riff upon listening ears. Cuts for your most basic musical urges include "Merry Go Round" and "Earth - shaker.' The James Gang; rock and roll never had it so good. SOMETHING IN MY LIFE - Tom Paxton - Private Stock PS 2002 - Producer: Kris O'Connor Tom Paxton's music is the music of the mo- ment; of good times and times that have passed long ago into the night. On his latest album Pax - ton's laidback guitar picking and tight backing unit add still more musical understanding via the light folk bag he's become the master of. Highlighted on this disk are "Gaining On Me" and the nostalgic look back on "My Daddy And Me." On all cuts Paxton's clear yet subtle singing style forms a tight bond with his material. When you're a craftsman. as Tom Paxton most certainly is. your music is your just rewards and. in this case. it's ours. LOVE LOVE LOVE - Jimmy Roselli - M&R C 1002 - Producer: Jimmy Roselli Jimmy Roselli has often been referred to as the "dynamic better" and based on this latest musical offering Roselli was well named. The key to Roselli's success is the pure uninhibited emotion that goes into his vocal interpretation. This he does very successfully on "Questions and Answers," "What A Difference A Day Makes" and "What Are You Doing To The Rest Of My Life." The overall production values on this re- cord are first rate as is the union between artist and material. Jimmy Roselli sings it and you feel it. pop picks JOAN; E1AEZ CiAMCYJs & RUST FANDANGO - ZZ Top - London PS 656 - Producer: Bill Ham Not since the early days of Cream has a power trio captured the raw rock and blues energy that ZZ Top has managed on this half live half studio outing. The economics of each cut, none over four minutes in length, services the perfect prov- ing ground for the pulverizing riffs of Billy Gib- bons and Dusty Hill. Frank Beard's neanderthal backbeat serves as a driving lead to the overall killer approach to the likes of "Balinese" and "Nasty Dogs And Funky Kings." ZZ Top means aggressive in any language and the world will be better for it. DIAMONDS AND RUST - Joan Baez - A&M SP 4527 - Producer: David Kershenbaum and Joan Baez Long noted for her incorporation of politics and social reform into the fiber of her songs; Joan Baez has done a turnabout with "Diamonds And Rust." The album contains narry a hint of political relevance but instead relies on in- trospection and human relationships as the guid- ing theme for the music. Ms. Baez is more than equal to the task as she treats her material and that of other writers with a tenderness and feel- ing conducive to a good listen. Joan Baez was once an advocate of politics of the mind. With "Diamonds And Rust" she has become a spokes- person for the politics of the heart. BEST OF FREE - Free - A&M SP 3663 - Producer: Free, John Kelly, Chris Blackwell, Guy Stevens One of the real tragedies of modern day popular music was the failure of Free to capture the top rung of stardom the band so richly de- served. The band. in its heyday, was the foreost practitioner of rock and blues on either side of the Atlantic. This best of an album is a fitting epitaph to the immense talents of the band that has since gone to its just rewards. From the opening riffs of Paul Kossoff on "All Right Now" through Paul Rodger's physical vocals on "Fire and Water," the band cooks as none may ever do again. A classic reminder of what has come and gone. Free; rest in peace. SONGS FOR A FRIEND - Jon Mark - Columbia PC 33339 - Producer: Jon Mark and Roy Halee "Songs For A Friend" comes across as being the same joy to listen to that it was for Jon Mark to record. This veteran musician (once a member of the cult English group "Sweet Thursday and the more jazz oriented Mark Almond), has put together a collection of haunting ballads that smack of countless human relations and untold life experiences. The intelligent use of strings plays an important part in Mark's overall musical presentation and their trade-off between vocals and piano prove a classic. Musicians are human too and this album proves it. SLIM CHANCE - Ronnie Lane - A&M SP 3638 - Producer: Ronnie Lane Its a decidedly different road that Ronnie Lane's walking on "Slim Chance." The former Face has totally immersed himself in a combina- tion of country, folk and blues that lends itself nicely to Lane's new found prowess as a vocalist. As this disk progresses even this mixture stretches out a bit as "Street Gang" captures a driving, horn backed calipso beat to turn in a spirited move number. Other cuts which offer new insight into Lane's true talents are "Little Piece Of Nothing" and the Dylanesque quality of "Anniversary.' Ronnie Lane's got a new face and he wears it well. THE GUITARS OF SONNY JAMES - Sonny James - Columbia KC 33477 - Producer: George K. Richey Sonny James does something with his music that only a skilled guitarist can do; he makes his style of playing go hand in hand with each in- dividual song. James' intricate picking is shown off to its best advantage in his instrumental cover of "Apache." Here, as in all other cuts, James makes his runs flow with the change in tempo and song pattern. Other outstanding James licks are exhibited on "Maria Elena" and "Eres Tu. - Sonny James is a ventriliquist of sorts; he makes his guitar speak and an oh so moving voice it is. May 10, 1975 19 www.americanradiohistory.com

cashbox,- news Nevins LP Bows Tom Cat Label NEW YORK - Rekease this week of the first album by Nancy Nevins heralds the debut of Tom Cat Records, the RCA - distributed record company headed by producer Tom Catalano. Ms. Nevins, a songstress who sang lead and wrote material for the rock band Sweetwater. is the first artist to be signed and recorded by Catalano. Catalano supervised Ms. Nevins' album in its entirety. Titled "Nancy Nevins." the album offers a collection of Ms. Nevins' own compositions. The LP was arranged and conducted by Artie Butler. Merchandising and sales promotion plans were announced for this LP by the label's marketing vice president. Sal Forlenza. A comprehensive campaign has been formulated that includes press kits. ad mats of various sizes. four-color FRONT COVER Motown's mighty Temptations have recharged one of the industry's most publicized legends with an energy - packed album, "A Song For You." which features the hit single "Shakey Ground." The result for the affectionately - proclaimed "Emperors of Soul." accord- ing to Motown, has been not only "im- mediate gold with platinum in sight," but a catalog explosion on previous Tempta- tions' "1990." "Masterpiece." and "All Directions," fueled by an extensive merchandising sales campaign. TV spots. posters. concentrated print and radio support have been only a part of the assault. A nostalgic frenzy of disco play and promotion have resulted in a Temptations re -discovery by a new generation of rhythm -oriented con- sumers. The Temptations today consist of Melvin Franklin. Otis Williams. Dennis Edwards, Richard Street and Glenn Leonard. They are currently in L.A. pre- paring a new stage extravaganza for one of the most ambitious world tours they've ever undertaken. Silvester, deCoteaux Sign With Chappell NEW YORK - Producer/writers Tony Silvester and Bert deCoteaux have signed a worldwide publishing and print agreement with Chappell Music Com- pañy. it was disclosed by Norman S. Weiser, president of the publishing com- pany. Included in the agreement between their Penumbra Music Company and Unichappell Music (BMI) isthe team's re- cent gold' record "Supernatural Thing" by Ben E. King (Atlantic). "Supernatural" is the title of King's just -released LP which was also produced by Silvester and deCoteaux. "We feel this is definitely one of Chap- pell's most significant moves in the con- temporary music area." said Norman Weiser. "Not only will we be working with two highly successful and diversi- fied writers, but also two very active pro- ducers." Formed in 1974, the team produced Sister Sledge's LP "Circle Of Love" (At - co) and their two hit singles "Love Don't You Go Through No Changes" and "Cir- cle Of Love." Their production of Martha Reeves' "Love Blind" has just been re- leased. In addition. they have released Mottola. Weiser, ter, de Coteaux product by Peter Nero (Arista), Ben Vereen (Buddah), Manu DeBango (At- lantic) and Jeree Palmer (Columbia), among others. The team has also un- dertaken projects with Linda Lewis (Arista). Bette Midler (Atlantic), Gary Glitter (Arista). Sam Dees (Atlantic). Ronnie Dyson, Les McCann (Atlantic) and The Voices of East Harlem (Mo- town). Before forming their production com- pany. both Silvester and deCoteaux had highly successful individual careers. Silvester helped form and was a member of the hit recording group The Main Ingredient. He co -wrote and produced many of the group's early records. Prior to their partnership, deCoteaux had been a producer and/or arranger for such major acts as Paul Anka, The James Gang, Willie Bobo and many others. One of his records was B.B. King's "The Thrill Is Gone," which garnered both a gold re- cord and a Grammy Award. He was also arranger for The Main Ingredients' gold record winners "Everybody Plays The Fool" and "Just Don't Want To Be Lonely." Silvester and deCoteaux have recently signed writers Gwen Guthrie and Patrick Grant to Penumbra Music. and they plan to produce Miss Guthrie. Rudell (seated), Silves - Olivia Re -Signs With MCA LOS ANGELES - Olivia Newton -John has re-signed with MCA Records. Inc. for a long term contract it was announced by Lee Kramer (Olivia's manager) and J. K. Maitland (president of MCA Records. Inc.) The signing took place on opening night of Olivia's sold out engagement at the Riviera Hotel in Las Vegas. In the past year, Olivia has earned no fewer than seven gold records and two platinum albums. The MCA LPs "Have You Never Been Mellow" and "If You Love Me, Let Me Know" reached platinum status. Olivia's MCA album titled "Let Me Be There" was certified gold and the single releases. "Let Me Be There." "If You Love Me. Let Me Know." "Have You Never Been Mellow" and "I Honestly Love You" were also certified gold. Olivia swept this year's music awards. winning more prizes in both country and pop classifications than any other female vocalist. Ms. Newton -John was the win- ner of four American Music Awards in the categories of Favorite Female Vocalist in Pop or Rock of 1974, Favorite Female Vocalist in Country Music of 1974. Favorite Album in Country Music of 1974 ("Let Me Be There") and Favorite Single in Pop or Rock of 1974 ("I Honestly Love You"). The Country Music Association named Olivia Top Female Vocalist of the Year. In addition. she was awarded two Grammies for "I Honestly Love You" as Record of the Year and for the same song in the category of Best Pop Vocal Performance for a Female. In the People's Choice Awards, Olivia Newton -John was named Favorite Female Singer of 1974. New Kirshner TV'er To Air Next Month NEW YORK - Jerome Schnur and Don Kirshner will be entering daytime television next month with "Musical Chairs" a new musical game show hosted by singer -actor Adam Wade. This musical variety show within a game show format premieres on the CBS television network on Mon.. June 16. and will be seen weekdays 4:00-4:30 p.m. EDT. Kirshner and Schnur revealed that "Musical Chairs" will be a showcase for emerging stars from the theatre. nightclubs and the recording industry. Two special guest stars will be in- troduced each week along with a singing group to assist Wade in delivering a variety of song lyrics. The contestants must choose the correct lyric as part of a three -round elimination to determine the winner. Kirshner helped to create a marketplace for rock music on television with shows like "The Monkees." "In Con- cert" and the current syndicated series, "Don Kirshner's Rock Concert." Schnur has been active in all phases of television for 25 years and is a former Peabody Award winner. The show will originate from New York. Kirshner. Wade. Schnur Epic, Magnet Ink Dist. Pact For U.S., Can. NEW YORK - Ron Alexenburg, vice president and general manager of the Epic and CBS custom labels, has an- nounced the signing of an agreement with Michael Levy, managing director of Magnet Records for the distribution of all Magnet releases in the United States and Canada. The first release under this deal will be a single entitled "There's a Whole Lot of Loving" by the British group Guys and Dolls. Under the terms of the new pact. all Magnet releases in the United States and Canada will be issued on the Epic label and will carry the Magnet records logo. In addition to Guys and Dolls, other acts will be added to the Epic roster from the Magnet stable of artists, with Epic re- taining first right of refusal on all Magnet recording acts in the U.S. and Canada. Magnet currently has four singles in the British top 40: "Hurt So Good" (Susan Cadogan). "Love Me. Love My Dog" (Peter Shelley), "Save Me" (Silver Convention). and "There's a Whole Lot of Loving" (Guys and Dolls). Alexenburg, Levy. ZurawinJoinsA&M LOS ANGELES - Effective immediate- ly, Iris Zurawin has joined A&M Records as merchandising manager for the label, announced Barry Grieff. director of merchandising. Ms. Zurawin was formerly the national singles sales manager for Epic and the Columbia custom labels in New York. Drosnes Named Buddah Veep NEW YORK - Mort Drosnes has been named administrative vice president of The Buddah Group. The announcement was made last week by Art Kass, presi- dent of the company. Kass explained that Drosnes' position is a newly created post with Buddah. Kass said, "Most important, from the standpoint of The Buddah Group. is that with Mort as administrative vice presi- dent. I will now have the flexibility to de- vote more time toother areas of our operations that demand more of my at- tention." Drosnes will report directly to Kass and will work closely with him primarily in the areas of business affairs and administra- tion, including the negotiation of artist/producer and publishing agree- ments. Drosnes comes to Buddah from the Ampex Corporation. where he was head of business affairs. Prior to joining Ampex as general attorney. Drosnes served eight years in the Columbia Records legal department where he became assistant general attorney. Mort Drosnes ASCAP Re-elects Adams, Officers NEW YORK - The board of directors of the American Society of Composers. Authors and Publishers has re-elected lyricist Stanley Adams as president. He has been a member of the ASCAP board of directors since 1944. and served as president from 1953 to 1956 and from 1959 to the present. An honorary member of the council of the American Guild of Authors and Com- posers (AGAC). Adams is a vice presi- dent of the National Music Council, a member of the board of trustees of the Great Neck Symphony Association, a vice president of the Country Music As- sociation. and has recently been elected to the administrative bureau of CISAC (International Confederation of Societies of Authors and Composers). The ASCAP board also re-elected Salvatore Chiantia (president of MCA Music) and three -time academy award - winning writer Ned Washington as vice presidents. Composer Morton Gould was re-elected to the position of secretary; Ernest R. Farmer (president of Shawnee Press, Inc.). treasurer; composer Arthur Schwartz, assistant secretary; and Leon J. Brettler (executive vice president of Shapiro. Bernstein & Co.. Inc.). assistant treasurer. cash box; country news RCA Adds 3 May Country LPs NASHVILLE - Dave Wheeler, RCA's national sales manager of country music. announced that RCA's spring country promotion called "Listen, America" con- tinues in high gear. In making the state- ment, Wheeler added that RCA will re- lease three more country albums under the program. The new May releases are: Dottie West's "Carolina Cousins." Hank Snow's "Easy To Love." and Porter Wagoner's "Sing Some Love Songs." Dottie's album comes in conjunction with Coca Cola's "Carolina Cousins" re- gional radio commercials which kicked off in the Carolinas recently. The album also contains "Country Sunshine" and "I'm Your Country Girl," both of which were used as Coke commercials in the past. Also included is Dottie's latest single. "Rollin' In Your Sweet Sunshine" and "Back Home Again." Hank Snow's "Easy To Love" album comes hot on the heels of his most re- cent single. The LP also includes"Merry Go Round Of Love." "I Almost Lost My Mind" and "Follow Me." Porter Wagoner's "Sing Some Love Songs" album includes "The Last One To Touch Me," "She's Everywhere" and his latest single. "Just For The Lonely Ones." The addition of the three May album releases brings the number of albums in- cluded in the "Listen. America" program to 16 releases plus the entire RCA coun- try catalog. The others are: Ronnie Milsap's "A Legend In My Time." Dolly Parton's "Bargain Store." Gary Stewart's "Out Of Hand." Elvis Presley's "Promised Land," Charley Pride's "Pride Of America." Chet Atkins' "Chet Goes To The Movies," Waylon's "Ramblin' Man." the new "Danny Davis Singers" LP. Bob- by Bare's "Hard Time Hungrys." Charlie Rich's "Greatest Hits." Jerry Reed's "Mind Your Love," Floyd Cramer's "Piano Masterpieces." and the two - record. 19 -song "In Concert" soundtrack album featuring: host Charley Pride. Chet Atkins. Ronnie Milsap. Dolly Parton, Jerry Reed and Gary Stewart. Magna To Handle Shannon Records Buffett Bookings Inks Intl Pacts NASHVILLE - Jimmy Buffett's ap- pearances, after June 1, 1975, will be booked by Magna Artists Corporation of New York City, stated Don Light, Buf- fett's personal manager. "Buffett's career is growing so fast, that it will require specialized attention both in booking as well as management. I'm going to concentrate on manage- ment, and we're going to assign the booking responsibilities to a well known, well respected major firm in New York. This will permit me to spend more time with Jimmy on the road," Light ex- plained. The Magna agent assigned to Buffett is Ed Rubin. Grammer Re -Signs /Monument Records NASHVILLE - Fred Foster, president of Monument Records, announced Bthat il- ly Grammer has been signed to a record- ing contract with the label. Grammer's signing marks a return to Monument Records after a fifteen year absence and a reunion with Fred Foster, his producer. On August 13, 1958. Grammer and Foster came to Nashville from Washington. D.C. to record the first session that was to launch the Monu- ment label. The result was "Gotta Travel On." a million seller for Grammer and the first of a long string of hits for Foster and his record company. Grammer left Monument under amicable circumstances in 1960, and now has re- turned with a new release "Family Man" scheduled for. coincidently. a May 13th release date. Upon re-signing, Grammer said. "this is for life." "I began with Monument and will end my recording career with Monu- ment." Clark Named Opry Grand Marshall NASHVILLE - Roy Clark has been named grand marshall for the 44th An- nual Rooster Day Celebration Parade May 17 in Broken Arrow. Oklahoma. Clark will also take part in the ceremony that day designating Broken Arrow an of- ficial bicentennial city. NASHVILLE - Mary Reeves Davis, pre- sident of Shannon Records. announced negotiations have been completed for international distribution. The arrange- ments will give the Shannon repertoire distribution in all the major world music markets. Contracts. negotiated by Shannon's in- t'l consultant, Dick Broderick. and Shan- non's general manager. Harry Jenkins. have been concluded with British Decca for the United Kingdom and Europe. RCA Records of Canada, Victor Musical Industries of Japan and RCA Limited of Australia. Initial international releases include the current chart -climbing single by Roy Head. "The Most Wanted Woman In Town," plus recent singles by Shannon artists George Kent, Bud Logan. Wilma Burgess. Harlan Sanders, Jimmy C. Newman and Nancy Ryan. Jackson Exits Bang Records Post ATLANTA - Wynn Jackson has. effec- tive immediately, resigned his position as promotion chief for Bang Records. While serving in promotion and artist de- velopment and marketing capacities at Bang, Jackson worked with such artists as Paul Davis, Ron Price and Pyramid, etc. According to Jackson, his future plans will be announced shortly. In the interim he can be reached at (404) 434-9814. Fan Fair '75 Alerts Fans NASHVILLE - The official sponsors of Fan Fair '75 have alerted businessmen and fans alike to watch out fot un- authorized sales of souvenir books, pro- grams. ads and/or personal accessories dealing with this year's Country Music Fan Fair. They stressed that official Fan Fair publications and accessories are handled only by representatives of CMA or the Grand Ole Opry. Unknown callers may be checked out by contacting the CMA at 244-2840; or the Grand Ole Opry at 749-1358. Country Artist Of The Week Kathy Barnes "Lucky Thirteen?" - Newcomer to the country charts is MGM's Kathy Barnes with her provocatively titled chart climber "I'm Available (For You To Hold Me Tight)". From her hometown of Henderson. Kentucky. Kathy, with her brother Larry. went the traditional route of school. social. civic and talent contests until she reached her "lucky" 13th birthday when everything good began to happen. Veteran Hollywood personality Smiley Burnett auditioned Kathy by phone and then through his belief in her ability brought her to the attention of Gene Autry. Smiley's confidence and belief was reinforced by Gene Autry and Kathy now enjoys the distinct status of being the only artist to become the protege of the legendary Mr. Autry. Kathy has studied drama at the Hollywood Professional Drama Academy and is a professional dancer. She has had national television exposure and her introduction to recording was made when she and brother Larry were pro- duced by Chet Atkins on the great stan- dard ' My Blue Heaven." Along with her MGM contract, Kathy Barnes is under exclusive personal management of Progressive Artist Management (PAM). a division of Burgess -Hale and Associates of Nashville. asnbox/album reviews FOUR WHEEL DRIVE -- Bachman-Turner Over- drive - Mercury SRM 1-1207 - Producer: Randy Bachman The highest compliment that can be paid to Bachman-Turner Overdrive is that they've worked more musical magic with the basic three J rock and roll chords than any band trotting the | boards today. Their growth and mastery of "girth | rock" is further evidenced on "Four Wheel | Drive" as the Canadian wrecking crew blitzkrieg j their way through the likes of "She's Keepin’ | Time" and "She’s A Devil." The Overdrive's bludgeoning approach to musical get down is ! akin, in a positive way, to McDonalds restaurant. It's as predictable as a Big Mac but oh so tasty. Bachman-Turner Overdrive — for the nean- derthal in you THERE’S NO PLACE LIKE AMERICA TODAY - Curtis Mayfield - Curtom CU 5001 - Producer: Curtis Mayfield Curtis Mayfield has a love affair going with the ghetto and it’s been the resultant musical in- terpretation of these life experiences that has led him to breaking new musical ground in the soul and rhythm and blues field. On "There's No Place Like America Today’Mayfield adds polish to his city music and comes up with a panorama of musical insights. Mayfield's songs take on the body of relationships that revolve around city liv- ing and yet on "So In Love" the process is as an oasis in the center of the rugged living edict Curtis Mayfield — the sounds of the city run through his brain. BANKRUPT - Dr. Hook - Capitol ST 11397 - Producer: Ron Haffkine Dr. Hook, the princes of absurdist and roll, are back with another fine mixture of music and cow dung that’s guaranteed to tickle every funny bone you’ve got. It's a delicatef?) balance this time out as the down home foolishness of "WUPS" and the band’s personal dance craze "Levitate" blend well with a surprisingly well done straight rendition of "Only Sixteen.” As always the talented songwriting insanity of Shel Silverstein plays an important part in the success of the Hook’s Capitol venture. To cop a song title in final compliment, “I Got Stoned And I Missed It ” Don't you. SPARTACUS - Triumvirat - Capitol ST 11392 - Producer: Jurgen Fritz Triumvirat has quickly become one of the most durable of the new wave of synthesizer rockers and with the release of "Spartacus" the reasons why have become crystal clear The band has evolved out of the strict classical adherence that limits most keyboard prominent bands and is put- ting its musical talents to work in areas closely al- igned to jazz and a higher, more polished rocking structure. Of particular note this outing is Jurgen Fritz’s soothing interludes on piano. Highlighted are "The March To The Eternal City" and The Hazy Shades of Dawn." Triumvirat — you de- serve this break today DESOLATION BOULEVARD - Sweet - Capitol ST 11395 - Producers: Phil Wainman, Mike Chapman, Nicky Chinn, Sweet Rock and roll has always been a good vehicle for describing the teenage dilemma In the case of the Sweet’s "Desolation Boulevard" — the Sunset Strip glitter, limpwrist crowd gets the band’s full attention via a series of alloy edged rock and roll cuts. Andy Scott’s raw lead riffs combine with Brian Connolly's frantic vocals to propell the music at the breakneck pace necessary for the effective representation of teenage mania that this record is Highlighted on this riff-infested outing are "Ballroom Blitz," "I Wanna Be Committed” and "Fox On The Run.” Desolation Boulevard; harder than you’ll ever be NO MORE CHANGES - Nicky Hopkins - Mercury SRM 1-1028 — Producers: Nicky Hopkins, John Edwards and Mark Smith Nicky Hopkins is a talented musician. His talent is attested to by major stars who’ve sought out his keyboard abilities on numerous oc- casions. So it was only natural that when Hopkins decided to do his own gig that the same excite- ment he brought to others would show up on his own grooves. Hopkins solo workout highlights an electrifying set too with his own material as well as that of his contemporaries and all work exceedingly well. Strong album cuts include "Sea Cruise,” "Last Night’s Changes," and "Lady It’s Time To Go.” poppicks GORILLA — James Taylor — Warner Bros. BS 2866 — Producers: Lenny Waronker and Russ Titelman Just plain good listens are few and far between And so it’s nice to know that James Taylor can be counted on to consistently turn out songs that are just that; which is the overriding theme of his latest on Warner Bros., "Gorilla." The sparse instrumental backing on all cuts pro- vides the necessary springboard for Taylor's natural countrified vocals to take command Taylor is equally at home on his as well as other people's compositions, with his polished coverof "How Sweet It Is (To Be Loved By You)" stand- ing tall on the scale of excellence he's always maintained James T aylor's “Gorilla” — you'll go ape over it TALE SPINNIN’ — Weather Report — Columbia PC 33417 - Producers: Josef Zawinul and Wayne Shorter The world of Weather Report is a mystical world of jazzical tones, wherein notes become chords and instruments take on harmonies normally reserved for lines of a human nature. It is a sphere of moments based in phases hellbent on being expressive and then, just as suddenly disappearing into the void; to be replaced by yet another music thought This latest trip into the world of Weather Report is yet another chapter in the ever growing book of living that is theirs. "Tale Spinnin 1 ” is music to be human to. Weather Report — to understand their music is to have arrived. MIDNIGHT ON THE WATER - David Bromberg Band — Columbia PC 33397 — Producers: Brian Ahern and Bernie Leadon David Bromberg's prowess as a guitar picker has placed him high on everybody's all around entertainer list. His interpretation of country music is an exercise in added depth and dimension that carries with it shades of the hills and of American music forgotten in the headlong rush of modern day living. All these pluses come to the fore in "Midnight On The Water” as Brom- berg and company run though a series of classic country cuts. Highlighted are a riverboat jazz laced "I Like To Sleep Late In The Morning" and a resonant vocal outing on "Nobody." David Bromberg — you need this album ANNIVERSARY SPECIAL, VOLUME ONE - The Earl Scruggs Revue - Columbia PC 33416 — Producer: Bob Johnston The Earl Scruggs Revue, along with a host of guest musicians, really kick out the jams on this country get down Earl’s above board banjo pick- ing proves the driving force behind a variety of country and hill songs that are at once en- trenched in a positive phase of musical Americana. Guest artists giving Earl a helping hand include Joan Baez, Johnny Cash, Billy Joel and Ken Loggins. Music such as "The Swimming Song” and "The Bleeker Street Rag” all have one thing in common; they'll get your toes to tap- pin' in a way they haven't done in many a moon The Earl Scruggs Revue — happy anniversary. NANCY NEVINS — Nancy Nevins — TomCat BYL 1-1063 — Producer: Tom Catalano Nancy Nevins, the initial release on Tom Cat Records, forms a musical combination of style and grit that is sure to find the mark. Ms. Nevins carries a strength in her vocals that is at once sophisticated and then, just as suddenly, sassy in a way that sends shivers down the listener’s spine This two-fold musical prowess makes its presence felt on "We Could Always Say It Was Rainin' " and gently shifting moods of "Lately .” Other cuts to sink your musical teeth into are “Just Like A Little Boy," "Ten Cents A Dance" and "Baroquen Heart " Nancy Nevins — the beginning of a star-studded career. FUSION II - Michal Urbaniak - Columbia PC 33542 - Producer: Michal Urbaniak Michal Urbaniak’s continued assault on all that is progressive in music is alive and well in "Fusion 11” as the Polish musician and his capa- ble cohorts break new ground on what were thought to be established musical boundaries. Urbaniak's violin is a veritable buzzsaw as it tears and distorts the various fibers of music to form yet another ongoing component of the musical prowess. Urbaniak and company touch off on new musical shores with cuts such as "Chinatown Part I,” "Bloody Kishka" and "Crazy Kid." Also good for a get down is "Kuyaviak Goes Funky." Michal Urbaniak — hardly a Polish hoke. 22 May 24. 1975

Police Brutality ANN ARBOR — Recording artists Blue Magic sustained injuries due to alleged brutality by Wackensaw county police of- ficers in Ann Arbor. Michigan on Satur- day. May 10 The group, who had an engagement Friday, May 9, in Muskeegon, Michigan, were enroute from a restaurant at the Howard Johnson's Hotel at Wackensaw and Carpenter Streets to their next gig in Erie, Pennsylvania The group alleges that upon leaving the restaurant in their car they were converged upon by ap- proximately ten police units The group alleges that the police jumped out of their cars and instructed the group (us- ing numerous obscene and racial references) to get out of their car At that moment, officers with rifles and pistols cocked, forceably removed the members of Blue Magic. Their driver, Charles Kel- ly, the first out of the car. was thrown to the ground Keith Beaton of Blue Magic was allegedly handcuffed while officers held cocked pistols in his face Soon the rest of the group were removed and handcuffed. At this point, officers allegedly en- gaged in a series of brutalities upon the members of the group An officer al- legedly crushed his boot into Ted Mills' (lead singer of Blue Magic) ankle with a gun pointed in his face as a dare and fright tactic. An officer allegedly hit Keith Beaton's spine with the butt of his rifle and an of- ficer allegedly kicked Richard Pratt in his face while he was on the ground handcuffed Mr. Magic Doing Magic On The Charts HOLLYWOOD — With multiformat air- play errupting across r&b, jazz, pop. pro- gressive and top-40 boundaries, sup- ported by a national SRO tour that has snapped house attendance records in several markets, Grover Washington, Jr.'s "Mr Magic" has become CTI’s big- gest selling album since the label’s in- ception. According to Tom Noonan, Motown’s director of marketing, the album is in ex- cess of 350,000 units and shows every sign of going gold this month. Currently topping the nation's jazz and soul charts, "Mr. Magic” is bulleting up pop charts with top-thirty placement in all three trades The recently released single. “Mr. Magic,” is starting to break both r&b and pop “What’s especially significant," commented Mike Lushka, Motown’s na- tional sales manager, "is that not only is Grover crossing over in many directions, but he’s introducing an entirely new au- dience to other CTI giants like Bob James, Ron Carter, George Benson and others.” Tempts Join Gemini Roster HOLLYWOOD — Ira Okun. executive vice-president of Gemini Artists Management Ltd announced the ex- clusive worldwide signing of theTempta- tions The Tempts, one of the most suc- cessful acts in all the world, have a cur- rent gold album with their latest on Motown, entitled "Song For You," and a hit single entitled "Shakey Ground." This is the fourth consecutive gold album for the group Gemini has set up a summer theatre tour for the group with a tour of Europe and Australia slated forthe fall. At this time, an officer tore away the pants of Wendall and Vernon Sawyer and continued his search None of the mem- bers of the group were advised of their rights or why they were being searched, according to Keith Beaton The musi- cians in Blue Magic's band, who were traveling behind the group in a van, were allegedly held spread eagle with rifles cocked and aimed at them by assisting officers. During this period, the group claims the following remarks were made by the officers One officer referring to another allegedly said “Can I shoot one of them?" "I'd like to take the dirt plow and plow them over to the police station" and allegedly made continuous harass- ing and racist statements using the word "nigger." After a series of phone calls, the sheriffs department became aware that the members were indeed the musical group Blue Magic and they were un- handcuffed and released Charles Kelly, their driver, was booked and released on $1,000 bail for possession of starter cap pistols. The group alleges that obviously, pending court hearing, no member of their aggregation carried any pistols or cap guns into the restaurant and that not only were they deprived of their con- stitutional rights but they were subject to racial and personal degradation. Upon leaving the station, the group im- mediately drove to Erie, Pennsylvania, where they were treated for their in- juries. A full investigation is pending by legal representation for Blue Magic. Carolina LOS ANGELES — The mayor of Morgantown, North Carolina, proclaimed May 16 "Johnny Bristol Day" when the MGM/Polydor Records artist was honored in his hometown by members of the Morgantown city council, chamberof commerce officials and county com- missioners, along with other top com- munity leaders. Have the numbers and chart positions that have been so important to AM radio affected FM pro- gramming for better or worse? Bruce Wende!!, National Promotion Manager, Capita! FM stations that are formatted similarly to top 40 sta- tions, are affected somewhat in the same manner as top 40 stations, which are very chart conscious. FM stations, with a broader programming spectrum, are more in- fluenced by the actual musical content rather than chart positions. However, whether it's an AM or FM station, a good chart position on any piece or product can only be beneficial. Bud O’Shea, Regional Promotional Marketing Manager, Epic and Custom Labels The term, FM radio, can no longer be identified with one particular type of format. When Tom Donahue start- ed the first "progressive FM station,'" KMPX, in San Francisco, chart positions, sales figures, etc., were the last things he would consider in adding a record His prime concern was if he felt the music was right for his station and audience. Since then, much like AM radio, many FM " progressive stations'" have become heavily formatted, only playing the "hits’. Stations with formats that add product, taking into consideration chart num- bers and sales, but mainly on the artistic value of product, are vital for ex- posure on new artists which is the lifeblood of the record business. One fac- tor which must be remembered is that you don't always receive maximum rotation on these stations. On the other hand, the tightly formatted station which relies very heavily on high chart positions and bullets tends to play fewer records which in turn gives you greater rotation. Both of these types of stations are essential to our industry. Records Linda Alter, National Promotion Director, Shelter Records The ever increasing role of the " numbers game" in radio today has begun to affect FM programming in much the same way as it did their AM competitors. With the added advantage of stereo broadcasting this change, in many cases, is building their audiences and increasing their ratings, which in turn makes those num- bers that much more important because everyone wants to play the ‘hits.’ FM's have unquestionably established their selling strength and have supplied the energy for the breaking of many new acts, which remains an impor- tant factor in the survival of the record industry. Paul Rappaport, Regional FM Promotion Manager, Columbia Records To a great extent, both retail research and chart awareness have been the tools which have helped FM radio really come into its own. However, this same re- liance on numbers has moved FM away from its tradi- tional role as an alternative to AM radio. While some “free form" stations still exist, and successfully, it would appear that in too many places the dollar is overshadow- ing the art Richard Chemel, FM & College Promotion Coordinator, 20th Century Records The majority of progressive stations I communicate with read the charts but are not affected as such when it comes to programming their station. The majority of FM programmers, progressively speaking, choose music which appeals to their audience. On the other hand, there are program and music directors that use charts in picking their music . . . chart positions are a useful tool when communicating with radio stations, as in publicity, promotion and overall marketing, the chart position is an integral part in the making and keeping of a hit record cashbox news MCA Reps Learn Manufacturing Techniques At East & West Sems HOLLYWOOD — Approximately 130 sales and promotion personnel from the MCA distributing organization witnessed the record manufacturing process at two seminars held week before last. Leroy Anderson Dies At Age 66 NEW YORK — Leroy Anderson, the composer of popular and light-classical music, died May 18 of lung cancer at his home in Woodbury, Conn He was 66 years old Among Anderson's best- known compositions are the wintertime standard “Sleigh Ride," written during an August heat wave, and "Blue Tango." which reached the #1 spot on the Cash Box charts 23 years ago this month. "Blue Tango” sold more than two million copies in 1952 and was the first in- strumental piece to reach the top posi- tion Another Anderson composition, "The Syncopated Clock” is used as the theme for the "Late Show” movies here All of Anderson's hits were instrumen- tals and usually featured familiar sounds, notably in "The Typewriter," and "The Sandpaper Ballet," which used different grades of sandpaper to duplicate the sound of vaudeville soft-shoe dancers. Among his other pieces are “Fiddle Fad- dle," "Jazz Legato,” “The Penny Whistle Song," "Forgotten Dreams,” “Promen- ade," "China Doll,” “Saraband," and Eire Suite." A study conducted by the American Symphony Orchestra League in 1953 found that Anderson was the American composer whose works were most frequently performed. Anderson once noted. “I never aimed for success or money or fame I just did what I wanted to do It turned out that people liked it." He is survived by his widow, the former Eleanor Jane Firke; three sons. Eric, Rolf and Kurt; a daughter, Jane; and a brother, Russell. Capito! ALBUM PREVIEW: An alumnus of Miles Davis and the jazz/rock group Dreams, Billy Cobham has made the transformation from a progressive rhythm and blues drummer to a top notch jazz percussionist-composer-arranger Since leaving the Mahavishnu Orchestra two years ago, he has released three albums under his own name with a fourth, "Shabazz." a live LP recorded at the Montreux Music Festival in Switzerland and the Rainbow in London to be released here on Atlantic next week With a seven piece band that included Michael and Randy Brecker on sax and trumpet, and John Abercrombie on guitar. Cobham built himself a formidable ag- gregate of talent to surround his own propulsive style of percussion which remains sizzling, sensuous, and direct He is perhaps at his best when playing a supportive role within the group; instigating and inciting the soloists on to greater improvisatory heights. Listen to Glen Ferris’ trombone followed by Abercrombie's guitar solo on “Red Baron (Revisited)” as they feverishly swell before they eventually soar Then listen to the undercurrents of rolling thunder created by Cobham's snare and tom- toms and the onrushing tidal waves of cymbals as they increase the fervent pitch of the composition. The overall sound quality of the live recording is excellent, though on the Montreux track ("Taurian Matador"), Cobham's drums are not miked as well as on the Rainbow takes Nevertheless, his playing is authoritive throughout as he shows that he is capa- ble of erupting into a torrid display of technique and energy He also ably demonstrates his ability to change the pulse of the music with a few well placed strokes. At the core of Cobham’s strengths and what makes his latest album so suc- cessful is his understanding of the music and his ability to translate his ideas into a loose, flexible sound. This is characterized by his compositions and the strong ensemble work which enhances his own consummate talents as a percussionist. barry taylor May 31, 1975 21

This costly, but probably effective technique, was the brainchild of trade vet and label chief Tom Catalano, known principally as an a&r maven but who is equal- ly steeped in marketing know-how thanks to years in the sales and promo stable of a major label As an a&r vet, Catalano's assault on record biz 1975 is also rather no-nonsense. He screened performances from over 1,500 acts before he selected the four (and only four) the new label will work with during their first year in business. The Tom Cat presence in the record business and its means of getting there is a textbook study in years of knowledge and experience applied to a changing industry, typified by high-concentration on a handful of artists, hand-crafted studio work and promotion saturation. VIBRATIONS - Albert Ayler - Arista AL 1000 Recorded in 1964 in Copenhagen at the Jazzhus Monmartre, this Albert Ayler record starkly portrays the many demons underlying his haunting music and his tragic life. Though the music on this record is clearly "outside," the im- portance of the basic melody line to Ayler is made perfectly clear Note especially, in this re- gard, the opening of "Ghosts." Ayler. however, is most adept at capturing music's visceral excite- ment. This instinctive quality is what gives the music its air of mystery With Don Cherry, Gary Peacock and Sonny Murray TANGERINE — Dexter Gordon — Prestige P 10091 Dexter Gordon was once called one of the most important tenor sax synthesizers of the bop and swing styles. His music is always solid, struc- turally inventive, and crisp One gets the feeling that an irrelevant note could never flow from his horn “Tangerine" includes naturally the Mercer- Schertzinger standard. "Days Of Wine And Roses," and two Gordon originals “August Blues" and "What It Was." On "Tangerine" and "Roses." Gordon demonstrates the jazzman's talent for taking an oft-heard melody line and making it a new harmonic and rhythmic creation. With Thad and Hank Jones, Stan Clarke, Louis Hayes, Cedar Walton, Buster Williams, and Billy Higgins. DIZZY GILLESPIE’S BIG 4 - Pablo 2310-719 One could make a strong argument that modern jazz had its beginnings in several small New York clubs in Harlem and on 52nd St One could be more specific and say that the revolu- tion began with a piece called "Be-Bop” by a young, bespectacled trumpet player named John Birks Gillespie Though the piece has rare- ly been played since the early 50s, Diz re- recorded it in 1974 with Joe Pass. Ray Brown, and Mickey Roker "Be-Bop” is more than a his- torical relic, though. The piece here retains its exuberance and vitality. THE ROADS FROM RAGS TO JAZZ - The New England Conservatory Ensemble - Golden Crest CRS 31042 The ragtime phenomena has for the most part been a played-out. a historical, commercial ripoff However, Gunther Schuller and the New England Conservatory Ragtime Ensemble show us clearly the historical significance of ragtime by portraying its connections with later jazz and earlier classical forms. The important point is that the line between these musical genres is not a fine but a blurred line. The Ensemble utilizes the compositions of Scott Joplin. Charles Ives, Erik Satie. Jelly Roll Morton, and Joseph Lamb to point out several vital constants in our musical heritage. 30 May 31, 1975

cashbox/news Rock In Politics: Governor Jerry Brown Picks Top In Pop HOLLYWOOD — Last week in the Los Angeles Times it was reported that pop music has seeped into the upper echelon of California state government. Specifically, Gov. Jerry Brown has been making both political and musical changes since his election. Alternately referred to as Sacramento Rock, Brown's selections include a variety of sound, from Linda Ronstadt to Gregorian chants. Brown, 37, announced during his cam- paign that he was a Ronstadt fan, that the chant is his favorite music, and that the Sufi Choir is perhaps the most inspiring musical group he's been associated with. After he won the election, Brown sat with the Sufi Choir for over two hours chanting and singing with them before going on to his victory party The MOR repertoire that was so popular during the Reagan era is no longer and Brown now plays his favorite pop music from 9 to 5 The artists include the likes of Ronstadt, Judy Collins, Ravi Shankar, Helen Reddy, Isaac Hayes and Carole King. The music, which is heard in certain areas of the Capitol and sur- rounding park, has attracted a lot of at- tention including some from State Treasurer Jesse Unruh who recently asked the Governor for more country and western selections. The influence of pop music on key figures in government has yet to be de- termined. but one can certainly see that the attendant atmosphere in Sacramento must be more relaxed as a result of the music's being played in select locations. Brown said recently that he had added Joni Mitchell and Tom Scott to his list of favorites and was very interested in the latter's recent performance at Holly- wood's Roxy Theatre Hopefully, the trend towards playing pop music in hallowed government halls will continue Whether or not we will see New York Mayor Abe Beame doing the bump down Broadway is doubtful, but the political climate across the land might improve noticeably with the addition of the best that pop music hastooffer. Following isa list of Brown's Top of the Pops: "East Meets West," Yehudi Menuhin and Ravi Shankar, "In A Silent Way,” Miles Davis, "Adagio for Strings and Concerto Cinque," Tomasso Albinoni, "Wildflowers.” and "Recollections" by Judy Collins, "Heart Like A Wheel” and "Don't Cry Now" by Linda Ronstadt, "Songbird" by Jesse Colin Young, "Silver Fox," "Inside" and "Inside II” by Paul Horn, The World of Tammy Wynette," "Free And Easy," Helen Red- dy, "Hot Buttered Soul," Isaac Hayes, Tapestry," and "Crying For Joy," The Sufi Choir. Four Gregorian chants are included: Missa Luba,” "Missa Flamenca and Mis- sa Maserabki." "Le Chante Gregorien Em L Abbaye de Kergonan Vol 2" and “Gregorian Chants Septuagesima." For classical music fans the Governor plays Beethoven Symphonies No 6, No. 3, No 7, No 9; Mozart Piano Concertos No. 21 and No. 24, Symphonies No. 40 and No. 41; and Bach "Brandenburg" Concertos No 4, No. 3, and No. 6 Transfer Lands CBS-TV Series NEW YORK — CBS television has signed The Manhattan Transfer to star in a series to run the last four weeks of the summer '75 season. Shows will air on Sundays beginning Aug. 10. The ex- ecutive producers will be Aaron Russo and Monte Kay, with a producer and a director to be named. The group has recently been appear- ing in major clubs around the country, in- cluding New York's Reno Sweeney’s, The Carlyle and The Bottom Line, The Bijou in Philadelphia, L A ’s Roxy and The Boarding House in San Francisco. They recently released their first album on Atlantic, entitled "The Manhattan Transfer," which is bulleted this week at i #70 on the Cash Box LP chart. Manhattan Transfer consists of vocalists Tim Hauser, Laurel Masse, Alan Paul and Janis Siegel, performing music which is derived from the blues, swing and jazz. The TV shows are scheduled to go into production at the CBS television studios in Hollywood dur- ing the month of July. Conn At Columbia, he was responsible for the transition of CBS Records distributors to branch de- pots and sales offices In October 1974, Craigo was named vice president of marketing Craigo HOLLYWOOD — Flash, theatrics, just plain fun, just plain weird. These are among the numerous tags that have been heaped upon practitioners of the musical art who have made the visual aspects of their performance as impor- tant as the music itself Whether or not the applied use of visual presence as an adjunct to one’s music is valid is a mute point The fact remains that there are quite a few musical units into stage theatrics and record companies are snapping them up with surprising reg- ularity. This theory has been put to practical use at Atlantic Records who boast among their stable of pop eccentrics Alice Cooper and recent acquisition Hawkwind The former's mastery of the bizarre in stage shows is unique while the latter’s presence (a science fiction dance macabre complete with psychedelic lights and a topless dancer) is a delightful throwback to the acid days of San Francisco in 1966-67 Bob Emmer, director of publicity for Atlantic, explained the reasoning behind the two acts being signed "There's no real mystery as to why we signed them Alice is a top entertainer and has a proven sales record He's the master of weirdness in popular music He does all those bizarre things in a positive way and. as a result, always put together an entertaining show "Hawkwind also puts on a highly visual and entertaining show and, over the years, they've really progressed as musi- cians The band has had great success in the midwest." In the case of Kiss; Casablanca Rec- ords has come up with the ultimate in theatrical overkill. The band, a by- product of thermonucleur heavy metal fallout, combines the hardest of rock with smoke bombs, blow torches, lights, sirens, rocket firing guitars, fire- breathing, dripping blood and all manner of mondo-bizarro props The resultant mind numbing and the band's coming under Casablanca's wings is explained by the label's Larry Harris: "First of all we weren't aware of Kiss's theatrical trip when we signed them. The music was good and the initial decision to sign was based on that. The theatrical things that the band does are a combina- tion of the ideas that the band had all along combined with some ideas that came out of the company." Harris continued; "The band is de- finitely theatre oriented but it's not the weird kabuki type thing a lot of critics are tagging them with The members of Kiss are into a more spacey type of presenta- tion and, if you had to put a label on what they were doing, I would call it science fiction rock. They're definitely leaning in that direction but the entire concept is theatre in rock music." Harris went on to say that people want more out of a live performance than just a bunch of musicians standing on a stage playing their instruments. "People want more than just music and that's why shows like the ones put on by Kiss are a valid part of show business." One cannot mention rock theatrics without paying overt homage to the Columbia-Epic combine who boast the tandem rock and roll blitzkreg, Blue Oyster Cult and The Dictators. Epic publicist Pat Siciliano, who prides himself as being a student of rock and roll eccentricities, explained the finer aspects of his heavy metal charges. "It's like the bands represent totally different and highly accessible areas in rock theatrics The Blue Oyster Cult has that heavy black leather trip, coupled with implied storm trooper tendencies going for them That appeals to one type of audience The Dictators are into a whole different thing. They combine the best parts of the slapstick of big time wrestling with all the ideas you've ever had about a punk garage band." Siciliano went on to explain that both bands from the New York school of rock have achieved a kind of underground status that has been a natural in terms of advertising and merchandising. The ob- vious question in terms of theatrics in music is measured at the cash register. While record companies are hesitant about giving out exact figures; the fineries of success are quite evident. Blue Oyster Cult is a constant member of chart upper reaches as is Alice Cooper Kiss, in a little more than a year, has risen to headline status in many sold out shows while Hawkwind and The Dic- tators seem on the verge of duplicating the success of their theatrical fore- bearers. But beyond figures of sales there is another area of proof — the street What are the kids paying good money to see? As is always the case, actions speak louder than words. Harrison Tunes Via I. AFM Approves New Commercials Pact NEW YORK — Affected members of the American Federation of Musicians have voted 637 to 188 to approve a new con- tract covering their services for TV and radio commercial announcements, it was reported by federation president Hal C. Davis. In response to the desires of local unions and player representatives, the major focus of the negotiations was in the areas of re-use, new use and dub- bing "We strongly feel that this agree- . ment will greatly increase the income of our members without jeopardizing their opportunities for employment in new production," Davis noted The two-year contract is retroactive to May 1 Among the primary changes and im- provements are as follows: For "dub- bing," "new use,” or "re-use,” a fee amounting to 621/2% of the applicable scale will now be paid, as opposed to a previous payment of 50%; Health and Welfare payments are increased from $2 to $3, and are payable for each session, rather than each contract; commercial announcements not exhibited for two years or more may only be shown upon payment of full scale in effect at the time of reactivation; payments for foreign use now only allow use for a 12-month, rather than 18-month, period without ad- ditional payments In addition, leaders contractors and orchestrators receive double the listed rates for foreign use Negotiators for the union and the joint policy committee of the Association of National Advertisers/American Associa- tion of Advertising Agencies had an- nounced tentative agreement on May 2. subject to approval by mail referendum of the musicians involved Si Mael New ABC VP HOLLYWOOD — Si Mael has been ap- pointed to the newly created position of financial vice president of ABC Records. He will report directly to Rubinstein, ABC Records' chairman Originally a CPA in public accounting practice, Mael gained recognition in the music industry as controller at United Artists, where he eventually became vice president and general manager.
